questions.description: Questions to ask the user (1-4 questions)

question.description: The complete question to ask the user. Should be clear, specific, and end with a question mark. Example: "Which library should we use for date formatting?" If multiSelect is true, phrase it accordingly, e.g. "Which features do you want to enable?"

header.description: Very short label displayed as a chip/tag (max 12 chars). Examples: "Auth method", "Library", "Approach".

options.description: The available choices for this question. Must have 2-4 options. Each option should be a distinct, mutually exclusive choice (unless multiSelect is enabled). There should be no 'Other' option, that will be provided automatically.

label.description: The display text for this option that the user will see and select. Should be concise (1-5 words) and clearly describe the choice.

description.description: Explanation of what this option means or what will happen if chosen. Useful for providing context about trade-offs or implications.

preview.description: Optional preview content rendered when this option is focused. Use for mockups, code snippets, or visual comparisons that help users compare options. See the tool description for the expected content format.

multiSelect.description: Set to true to allow the user to select multiple options instead of just one. Use when choices are not mutually exclusive.

answers.description: User answers collected by the permission component

annotations.description: Optional per-question annotations from the user (e.g., notes on preview selections). Keyed by question text.

preview.description: The preview content of the selected option, if the question used previews.

notes.description: Free-text notes the user added to their selection.

metadata.description: Optional metadata for tracking and analytics purposes. Not displayed to user.

source.description: Optional identifier for the source of this question (e.g., "remember" for /remember command). Used for analytics tracking.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background.

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to modify

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences of old_string (default false)

tools.name: ListAgents
tools.description: Lists agents you can SendMessage to — in-process subagents you spawned, the teammates on your team, other local Claude sessions on this machine, your Claude sessions running in the cloud (when this session has cloud access; a cloud session receives your message but cannot message any session back yet — do not ask it to reply, read its answer in its own transcript), and (when Remote Control is connected here) your account's other sessions — Remote Control sessions on other machines and cloud sessions, each row labeled by kind. Names are the address: send with `SendMessage({to: "<name>", message: "..."})`, copying the name exactly as a row prints it. Append a row's ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — two rows share it, or an error asks you to disambiguate.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ReportFindings

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

1	---
2	name: long-context-prefill-128k
3	description: "Prefill against depth out to 128k after P14 (2026-09-22): 826 tok/s at ubatch 2048 and 946 at 8192, the four changes, the four measured refusals, and the fast 4-layer probe."
4	metadata: 
5	  node_type: memory
6	  type: project
7	  originSessionId: 80f71c47-a621-4724-a77a-e285f8d84b61
8	  modified: 2026-09-22T11:38:44.739Z
9	---
10	
11	**128 000 cells prefills at 826.0 tok/s at ubatch 2048 and 946.1 at
12	8192 — `GOALS.md`'s 900 is met.** P13 left it at 563.6. 48 layers, shipped banks,
13	`wiki.test.raw`, one sequence walked forward, `-tg 8 -ctx 139000`. Write-up
14	`research/p14-prefill-at-depth.md`.
15	
16	| depth | P13 pp | P14 pp | | decode |
17	|------:|-------:|-------:|----:|-------:|
18	| 0 | 1129.3 | 1154.2 | 1.02x | 29.31 |
19	| 32 000 | 825.8 | 915.6 | 1.11x | 25.80 |
20	| 64 000 | 719.6 | 892.1 | 1.24x | 24.46 |
21	| 96 000 | 607.9 | 832.3 | 1.37x | 22.80 |
22	| **128 000** | **563.6** | **826.0** | **1.47x** | 22.18 |
23	
24	Falloff from depth zero **0.50x → 0.72x**. Against the ubatch at 128 000 alone
25	(two runs each): 826.0 at 2048, 886.1 at 4096 (the shipped
26	`-llm-batch`), **946.1 at 8192** — P12's trade at depth, so 8192 is a
27	batch summariser's setting. **Decode is the control and did not move.**
28	
29	**Four changes.**
30	
31	1. **The selection runs over block scores, not the expanded per-cell tensor**
32	   (`llm_attn_selblk.comp`). All `ratio` cells of a pooled block carry one score,
33	   so a weighted select over `nKV/ratio` entries is the same threshold, ties and
34	   bitmask. `attn.select` 0.281 → **0.020** (13.8x), `attn.expand` deleted, and
35	   **1.14 GB of arena** freed at ubatch 2048. Bit-identical, gated by
36	   `TestAttnGPUSelectBlocksIsTheCellSelect` over four chunk schedules.
37	2. **The attention runs over a per-cell gather** (`llm_attn_gather.comp` +
38	   `llm_attn_wmma.comp -DGATHER`). Per query tile, the union of its rows'
39	   selections compacted ascending, with the causal test folded into a per-row
40	   mask over the gathered positions. `attn.attn` 1.024 → **0.454** (2.15x on the
41	   4-layer probe; 0.566 → 0.303 at 48 layers). **The value plane had to become
42	   cell-major first** — a selected run is `ratio` consecutive cells, one
43	   128-byte line, where transposed it was four halves out of sixteen rows. That
44	   costs the block kernel ~7% and decode nothing.
45	3. **The indexer's score on the matrix cores** (`llm_attn_score_wmma.comp`). It
46	   is a GEMM per indexer head with a rectifier: 0.077 → **0.034**. Chunk-invariant
47	   (a matrix product's rows are independent), and *nearer* llama.cpp's selection
48	   than the scalar kernel (9760 vs 9762 of 6 298 621).
49	4. **`checkBufferRange`** — see [[a-benchmark-that-gets-faster]].
50	
51	**The gather is the first kernel here that is not chunk-invariant and cannot be
52	made so.** Its list is the union of a query tile's sixteen rows, so a chunk
53	ending inside the tile gathers a different list and the online softmax folds the
54	same terms in a different order. It is off under `Graph.PinSchedule` with the
55	other reassociating kernels, and the chunk-equality gates pin it (`SetGather`).
56	A prompt prefilled twice at the same ubatch is still bit-identical; only changing
57	the ubatch moves the last places. Gates: `TestAttnGPUGatherSelectsTheSameCells`
58	(exact on the set), `TestAttnGPUGatherIsTheBlockKernel` (4.1e-06 rms against
59	9.9e-04 from llama.cpp), `TestAttnGPUGatherRungsAgree`,
60	`TestAttnGPUGatherIsDispatched`.
61	
62	**The union is the number that prices all of this, and P13's estimate of it was
63	wrong.** `AttnGPU.SelUnion` measures it: at 128 000 cells a 16-row tile reads
64	**15 145** cells where its rows' union is **7 049** and one row selects 2 051.
65	The gather is therefore 2.15x, not the 3.3x P13 projected, and the 3.4x between
66	the union and one row is the floor a 16-row fragment cannot reach.
67	
68	**What the gathered kernel is bound by, by elimination** — four arms, all
69	1.00x-ish, in [[prefill-rates]]: not the matrix cores (doubling their work costs
70	2.7%), not the barriers, not the gather's own traffic (sharing it across two
71	heads buys 4%). It is the LDS round-trip for the fragments and the per-head
72	softmax scaffolding, both linear in the union.
73	
74	**The fast loop is still `-depth ... -layers 4`, 40 seconds an arm** — and it
75	**overstates** `attn.attn` because its one attention layer is denser than the
76	48-layer mean (19.0% live at bm16/bn16 against 11.7%). Ratios reproduce;
77	absolutes do not.
78	
79	    /tmp/pp -model $M -depth -depths 0,64000,128000 -pp 2048 -tg 4 -ctx 136000 -layers 4
80	
81	**Control arms**: `LLM_ATTN_GATHER=0`, `LLM_ATTN_GATHER_KERNEL=qt1_kt1|qt1_kt4`,
82	`LLM_ATTN_GATHER_GRP`, `LLM_ATTN_GATHER_HEADS`, `LLM_ATTN_EXPAND_CELLS=1` (also
83	what `Cells()` needs), `LLM_ATTN_SCORE=scalar`.
84	
85	**The whole-model check.** Three of the four changes claim bit-exactness, and
86	`TestGraphLogits` confirms all three at once: its diagnostics come back
87	byte-identical to the base (`maxAbs 2.507e+00 at 141557`, `rms 5.148e-01`, the
88	same top ten) through all 48 layers. Its *failure* is the pre-existing one — see
89	[[llm-test-suite-gotchas]], and note that a relative `LLM_BANK_CACHE` there
90	writes 23 GB into `llm/models`, which this session walked into.
91	
92	See [[prefill-rates]], [[context-depth-rates]], [[a-benchmark-that-gets-faster]],
93	[[llm-bench-needs-bank-cache]], [[never-edit-source-during-a-sweep]],
94	[[strix-halo-bench-runs]], [[graphstats-kinds-aliases]].

105	**Quote this table for decode — P16's (2026-09-22), not P15's.** 48 layers,
106	shipped banks, `-pp 2048 -tg 16 -ctx 139000`, `wiki.test.raw`, two passes to
107	0.3%, write-up `research/p16-decode-arena-width.md`.
108	
109	| depth | pp tok/s | tg tok/s | P15 tg |
110	|------:|---------:|---------:|-------:|
111	| 0 | 1155.8 | **34.39** | 29.73 |
112	| 8 000 | 973.9 | 33.54 | 28.78 |
113	| 32 000 | 919.7 | 33.20 | 28.72 |
114	| 64 000 | 896.3 | 32.41 | 28.14 |
115	| 128 000 | 834.4 | **31.53** | 27.20 |
116	
117	At ubatch 4096 (`-ctx 141000`, three depths — five overflow the descriptor):
118	0 → 1292.5 / 33.01, 64k → 979.4 / 33.00, **128k → 904.6 / 31.63**.
119	
120	**P16's lesson, which generalises: a knob that costs decode is found by a
121	per-label diff between the two arms, not by theorising.** The wide-arena cost
122	was blamed on memory residency for two passes (P12-7, P15); `-depth -ubatch`
123	(arena rows separate from `-pp`) showed it followed the arena, and the label
124	diff put all of it on `move`, `dn.qkv`, `attn.qkv` in one look — the input
125	ports padded a one-row decode step with zeros to the whole arena. A padding
126	that is *correct* and slow is invisible to every tolerance test; it is gated
127	now by `TestInPortPadsTheRunNotTheArena`. Also P16: `hc.cn` runs a workgroup a
128	(token, stream) at ≤ 64 rows (`LLM_HC_CN_SPLIT_ROWS`, 0 = P11's grid), and
129	`attn.select`'s emit walks blocks (68 → 55 µs at 128k); its passes are neither
130	load-latency- nor atomic-contention-bound (both measured, 0.96x and 0.69x).
131	
132	**The P15 section below still stands for what it explains** (the four depth
133	terms), with P16's rates on top.
134	
135	**A deep decode step is four terms and nothing else.** Every other kernel in
136	the model is flat in depth — `moe.up` 5.44 ms a token at both ends, `dn.qkv`
137	4.39, `hc.cn` 2.33. At 128 000 cells, base → final:
138	
139	- `attn.attn.split` 4.109 → **1.571** (the gather+split, P15-3)
140	- host `gather`, i.e. `PLERows` 5.175 → **1.263** (P15-1)
141	- `attn.score` 2.533 → **0.995** (the stripe at 64, P15-2)
142	- `attn.select` 0.862 → **0.862** — untouched, and now the largest
143	  depth-scaling term left on the device
144	
145	**The largest one was on the host.** `PLERows(cfg, g.ids)` hashed the whole
146	sequence every token and sliced off the tail — 8.2 MB allocated and 2.05 M rows
147	per step at 128k to use sixteen. `PLERowsFrom` is the tail-only form and is
148	exact by construction. The `-depth` bench had been printing that as a `gather`
149	line growing 3.1% → 11.7% with depth for as long as it has existed. **Read the
150	host lines of the profile, not only the kernel ones.**
151	
152	**The control knobs**, all env, all on `cmd/llm -depth`:
153	
154	    LLM_ATTN_GATHER=0            # P8's block split, which is what decode had
155	    LLM_ATTN_GATHER_MIN=<cells>  # the depth the gathered arm turns on at
156	    LLM_ATTN_CELL_SPLITS=16      # P9's stripe count, shipped at 64
157	    LLM_ARENA_UNCACHED=1         # the arena memory type
158	    LLM_NO_PRERECORD=1           # re-record every decode step
159	
160	**The gates after touching any of this** (plus P7-P10's, in
161	[[context-depth-rates]]):
162	
163	    go test ./llm/ -run TestPLERowsFromIsTheTail                   # exact
164	    go test ./llm/ -run TestAttnGPUGatherSplitIsTheGather          # tolerance
165	    go test ./llm/ -run TestPrerecordedDecodeCrossesTheGatherBound # the epoch
166	
167	**Two traps this pass walked into, both worth remembering.** A split-kernel
168	test that uploads the whole fixture at once passes with 0.000e+00 on every arm,
169	because `attnSplits` refuses any batch wider than `attnSplitMaxRows` — a split
170	that never engaged looks exactly like a perfect one, so assert on a zero. And
171	the obvious test for the prerecord epoch — diff the logits across the bound
172	with the replay on and off — **cannot fail**, because below the selection's
173	2051-cell width the gathered and block kernels are bit-identical; assert the
174	mechanism (`preEpoch` against the depth) instead.
175	
176	**How to apply:** needs `LLM_BANK_CACHE` — see [[llm-bench-needs-bank-cache]],
177	[[strix-halo-bench-runs]], [[never-edit-source-during-a-sweep]] and
178	[[llm-resident-run]]. The fast loop is `-depths 128000 -pp 2048 -tg 8 -layers 4`,
179	~60 s an arm, and it reproduces the `attn.attn` ratios to the microsecond.

197	| depth | base (P7) | +P8+P9 | +P8+P9+P10 | pp |

265	name: prefill-rates
266	description: "Prompt-processing rates after P12 (2026-09-21), the ubatch curve and the decode cost that comes with it, what the MoE prefill GEMM is bound by, and the four prefill ideas that are measured dead."
267	metadata: 
268	  node_type: memory
269	  type: project
270	  originSessionId: d77f87a5-b722-4ac5-aaa9-d322f713f1da
271	  modified: 2026-09-21T22:34:23.069Z
272	---
273	
274	**Prefill does not plateau where llama.cpp's does, so the ubatch is a real
275	knob — but widening it is a trade, not a free win.** 48 layers, shipped banks,
276	two runs each (`results/p12_pp_*.csv`, write-ups `research/p11-prefill.md` and
277	`research/p12-prefill-round-two.md`):
278	
279	**Superseded at depth by P14 (2026-09-22)** — see [[long-context-prefill-128k]]
280	for the rates against context depth, which are no longer these. The depth-zero
281	ladder below stands.
282	
283	| ubatch | P11 | P12 | vs llama.cpp |
284	|---:|---:|---:|---:|
285	| 512 | 681.7 | 683.3 | 1.75x |
286	| 2048 | 1191.8 | **1207.7** | 3.08x |
287	| 4096 | 1340.7 | 1363.5 | 3.48x |
288	| 8192 | 1372.2 | **1403.9** | **3.59x** |
289	
290	Against **context depth** at ubatch 2048: 1154.6 / 968.1 / 894.3 / 805.7 /
291	**667.7** tok/s at 0 / 8k / 16k / 32k / 64k. Arms are reproducible to
292	0.1-0.5%, so a 1.2% difference is real; quote means of two passes.
293	
294	**`-llm-batch` defaults to 4096 and, since P16 (2026-09-22), a wider batch
295	costs memory and nothing else.** P12-7 measured 4096 costing 8% of decode
296	through the server and P15 11-22% at depth; **that was a bug** — the DeltaNet
297	and attention input ports zero-padded a decode step out to the whole arena.
298	Fixed, through the server (four ~4k prompts, 256 generated, two passes to 0.1%):
299	
300	| batch | prefill | decode |
301	|---:|---:|---:|
302	| 2048 | 1052.2 | 34.19 |
303	| 4096 | 1198.5 | 34.20 |
304	| 8192 | 1232.5 | 34.16 |
305	
306	8192 only helps prompts > 4096 tokens, holds ~3 GB more, and lowers the
307	`maxStorageBufferRange` context cap. See [[decode-at-depth-after-p15]].
308	
309	**The MoE prefill GEMM is bound by its per-tile slab unpack, not by rows.**
310	Measured four ways in P11 (row padding 1.90x → 1.19x is worth *nothing*; a
311	per-fragment bound, three sub-lists, and BM 128 all lose). So the way to speed
312	`moe.up` up is fewer tiles at the same block width = fewer experts touched = a
313	bigger ubatch. P12 adds the floor: **gutting the whole Q4_K scale path is only
314	1.21x**, and what remains after the loads are collected — an int→float
315	convert, an FMA and an f16 convert per weight — has **no bit-exact cheaper
316	form** (packed fp16 costs ~13 bits of mantissa; `v_cvt_pkrtz` rounds toward
317	zero). At 21.1 TFLOP/s and 61 GB/s of bank it is neither matrix-core- nor
318	bandwidth-bound.
319	
320	**What is measured dead (do not re-attempt without new information):**
321	
322	- **Four arms on the gathered attention kernel, P14 (2026-09-22)**, and together
323	  they say what it is bound by. *Doubling the QK matrix work costs 2.7%*, so the
324	  matrix cores are ~5% of it. A subgroup staging barrier instead of a workgroup
325	  one is **1.00x**; staging two head-dim groups a barrier is **1.00x** and four
326	  is **0.75x**; putting two query heads in one workgroup so they share the staged
327	  key and value — which halves both the gather's global reads and its LDS writes
328	  — is **1.04x**, and four is **0.75x**. So it is not the matrix cores, not the
329	  barriers, not the gather's traffic and not occupancy-to-spare: what is left is
330	  the **LDS round-trip for the fragments and the per-head softmax scaffolding**,
331	  both of which scale with the union, which is why the kernel's cost is linear in
332	  the cells it visits. The 0.75x arms are LDS crowding out waves.
333	  `LLM_ATTN_GATHER_GRP` and `LLM_ATTN_GATHER_HEADS` are the ladders, both at 1.
334	
335	- **Compacting the live key blocks into a per-query-tile list is 1.00x at
336	  every depth** (P13, 2026-09-22) — it deletes 83% of the axis walk at 128k
337	  and `attn.attn` does not move. Third instance of the same rule, which is now
338	  the engine's and not any kernel's: *latency and redundant reads that matter
339	  at decode do not matter at prefill, because prefill has occupancy* — 3072
340	  single-wave workgroups against a decode step's 24. See
341	  [[long-context-prefill-128k]].
342	
343	- **`hc.cn`'s 256-way reduction tree costs nothing** — deleting it outright is
344	  5331.5 µs against 5325.8. The non-bit-exact subgroup rewrite P11 queued
345	  would have bought zero.
346	- **`hc.cn`'s per-token gamma read costs nothing** — replacing it with a
347	  constant is 5332.9 µs. It is 40 KB and the MALL serves it. Its 57% of copy
348	  bandwidth is now *unexplained and out of hypotheses*.
349	- **Hoisting the attention block skip out of the loop is 1.00x at every
350	  depth.** At 64k a query tile skips ~1480 blocks, each on a dependent global
351	  read; voting on the whole key range up front with a subgroup ballot buys
352	  nothing, because **a prefill dispatches 3072 single-wave workgroups where a
353	  decode step dispatches 24** — latency that matters at decode does not matter
354	  at prefill, because prefill has occupancy. The exact converse of P8. **Still
355	  live for decode**, where it was deliberately never built.
356	- **The selection mask loop is 3.5-8%** of the attention kernel, not the rest
357	  of the depth gap.
358	
359	**At depth the fast loop is `-depth -layers 4`, 40 seconds an arm**
360	([[long-context-prefill-128k]]) — `-attn` runs at `past = 0` and never
361	reaches depth's regime.
362	
363	**`cmd/llm -attn` is the fast loop for attention at depth zero and it is 1.9 seconds** (two
364	layers, real routing, real selection, per-label µs a layer) — use it, not the
365	7-minute `-graph` ladder. It tops out near 16 384 tokens (32 768 in one batch
366	trips P0's watchdog) and runs at `past = 0`, so it reaches the selection's
367	regime but **not depth's**; only `-depth` does. `cmd/llm -moe` is the MoE's
368	equivalent at 228 ms to stage. See [[context-depth-rates]] for decode,
369	[[llm-bench-needs-bank-cache]], [[never-edit-source-during-a-sweep]],
370	[[llm-test-suite-gotchas]].
371	---
372	name: decode-is-latency-not-bandwidth
373	description: "At decode this model's per-head GPU kernels are single waves that all fit on the device at once, so a dispatch costs one wave's serial walk — not its traffic and not its total work."
374	metadata:
375	  type: project
376	---
377	
378	**P8, 2026-09-21.** The probe that settles it: cutting the attention grid from
379	24 workgroups to 2 — a twelfth of the work *and* a twelfth of the traffic —
380	measured **1.00x at every depth** (0, 16 384 and 65 536 cells, three decimal
381	places).
382	
383	The reason is structural and applies well beyond attention. A decode step is
384	**one token**, so any kernel gridded on (query blocks, heads) or on (tokens,
385	…) dispatches a handful of workgroups; `local_size_x = WAVE` makes each one a
386	single wave; and this device has **40 compute units**. Everything launches at
387	once, nothing queues, and the dispatch's wall clock is the *longest single
388	wave's serial loop*. With one wave per CU there is nothing to hide a
389	`coopMatLoad`'s latency behind, which is why the measured rate was ~7 GB/s
390	where prefill on the same kernel achieves hundreds.
391	
392	So at decode:
393	
394	- **Adding parallelism across heads buys nothing** — they already run
395	  concurrently.
396	- **Removing redundant traffic buys nothing** — the redundant readers were
397	  never queued behind each other. (12 query heads share each of the 2 KV
398	  planes here and each re-reads it in full; deleting that is free and worth
399	  nothing.)
400	- **Only shortening the per-workgroup loop helps**, by splitting the reduction
401	  axis across more workgroups, or by making the loop's iterations fewer.
402	
403	Two kernels were fixed this way and a third is open — see
404	[[context-depth-rates]] for the numbers and `research/p8-decode-attention-split.md`.
405	`llm_attn_select.comp` is still one workgroup a token.
406	
407	**How to apply:** before optimising any decode kernel in this repo, check its
408	grid at `rows == 1` first. If it is tens of workgroups, the question is the
409	length of one wave's loop and *not* the bytes it moves — and the cheap probe
410	is to cut the grid and see whether the time moves at all. Do not reason from
411	bandwidth at decode; that reasoning is right at prefill and wrong here.
412	
413	**A prefill-shaped grid breaks this rule silently** (P16, 2026-09-22): P11
414	merged `hc.cn` to one workgroup a token for prefill bandwidth, which at decode
415	made it one workgroup walking four streams — 25 µs where a stream a workgroup
416	is 7. When a kernel is re-gridded for prefill, re-time it at `rows == 1`.
417

419	name: strix-halo-bench-runs
420	description: "How the strix-halo-vulkan benchmark suite is run and how long each family takes, plus the run-quality conventions the repo's docs expect."
421	metadata: 
422	  node_type: memory
423	  type: project
424	  originSessionId: 6c27486f-644d-4f43-a0b0-6ebe2136679b
425	  modified: 2026-09-18T12:55:03.680Z
426	---
427	
428	`go run ./cmd/bench -blocks 32,64,128,256,512,1024 <family>` — the non-default
429	block list is what every committed `results/*.csv` was measured with, so keep
430	it if rows are to stay comparable. `go generate ./...` first if any `.comp`
431	changed (`*.spv` is gitignored). As of 2026-09-13 the `moe` family is ~9
432	minutes / 896 rows; it prints its summary tables only at the end, so there is
433	no progress output to poll — run it in the foreground with a long timeout.
434	The `bank` family (added 2026-09-15, research/llm-vertical.md L0a) is the odd one out: its 72
435	timed cells are seconds, but `go run ./cmd/bench -bankgib 64 -bankreadmib 1024
436	bank` first allocates 64 GiB in 19 buffers and writes one word per 4 KB page,
437	which is most of its ~3-minute wall clock. Check `free -g` has the headroom
438	before starting it.
439	
440	**A whole-model tok/s number is only comparable against a control run the
441	same hour** (P1c, 2026-09-18): with an identical binary the decode step
442	measured 30.51 ms one day and 39.20 the next — every *dense-bank* kernel
443	1.6-1.9x slower (dn.qkv 115→206 us, head 1964→3531) while every MoE
444	expert-bank rung was unchanged. Suspected GTT page fragmentation of the
445	float-staged dense banks (32-day uptime, swap 100% full); unprovable without
446	root. **And a difference below ~0.5 tok/s needs interleaved A/B/A/B pairs, not one
447	pair** (P3, 2026-09-18): three pairs of the same two banks gave −0.06, +0.14
448	and +0.05 tok/s, so either single pair would have reported a signed number
449	where the truth was a within-arm spread of 0.31 against a real difference of
450	~0.04. Quote the means and the within-arm spread, not one delta.
451	
452	So when measuring a decode/prefill change, rebuild yesterday's code in
453	a worktree (`.spv` are gitignored — regenerate or copy them) and run both
454	binaries back to back; never quote a delta against a prior day's CSV. Also:
455	run 1 of a freshly staged graph diverges from runs 2+ at ~1.6e-5 in the
456	logits (research/p1c-prerecorded-decode.md finding 4) — warm the graph once
457	before any bitwise comparison.
458	
459	One-token `-ladder` runs of `cmd/llm` (moe/dn/attn/hc) must defeat the 32 MiB
460	MALL or every rate is an L3 number: stage many layers and use `-iters 1`
461	(e.g. `-moe -tokens 1 -ladder -layers 16 -iters 1`, P1b 2026-09-18 —
462	`ProfileSweep` walks a dispatch kind across layers, so each timing reads a
463	cold bank). The screen: any CSV row whose gbps exceeds 242 was not measuring
464	DRAM. The default two-layer, 20-iter form re-reads a ~32 MB working set from
465	the MALL.
466	
467	**`go generate` after a `.comp` edit is load-bearing, and skipping it fails
468	*silently and flatteringly*.** `.spv` is gitignored and embedded into the Go
469	binary, so an edited shader that was not regenerated runs the **previous**
470	kernel — and a hand-compile to `/tmp` to check syntax is not the same thing.
471	On 2026-09-19 (P5b) that produced a whole round of measurements that read as a
472	2x speed-up and a full set of green tests, because the old kernel was doing
473	half the work on the new grid. Regenerate just the families touched
474	(`grep "go:generate" shaders/shaders.go | grep <file>.comp | sed 's|^//go:generate ||'`
475	into a loop) and check the `.spv` mtime before believing any number.
476	
477	**Why:** the repo's TODO.md handoffs report a reproducibility figure for every
478	session (two runs of the family, median ratio and p10-p90 over common rows),
479	so a session that measures anything is expected to run its family twice and
480	quote the agreement.
481	
482	**How to apply:** budget ~20 minutes for two `moe` runs, save each log and CSV
483	to the scratchpad so run N-1 survives for the comparison, and check nothing
484	else is using the GPU (`/sys/class/drm/card1/device/gpu_busy_percent`) before
485	starting. **"Nothing else" includes your own `go build` and `go test`** — a
486	whole-model decode step is ~3 ms of host work in ~28, and compiling beside a
487	`-gen` run cost one control pass 1.6 tok/s of 35 (P4c, 2026-09-19), which is
488	four times the difference such a run is usually measuring. Start the
489	measurement detached (`setsid nohup … &`, or the foreground loop will kill it
490	when the tool call times out) and edit *text* while it runs, nothing else. Do not poll with `pgrep -f` — see
491	[[watch-loops-must-not-match-themselves]].
492	---
493	name: llm-bench-needs-bank-cache
494	description: "Benchmarking cmd/llm on the shipped banks needs LLM_BANK_CACHE set by hand, or every process start re-fits the MoE bank for eight minutes on all 32 cores."
495	metadata:
496	  type: project
497	---
498	
499	**`cmd/serve` sets `LLM_BANK_CACHE`; `cmd/llm` never does** (the comment at
500	`cmd/serve/main.go:177` says so outright). So a `cmd/llm` run launched with
501	`LLM_MOE_BANK` at the shipped plan but no cache path re-fits `ffn_down_exps`
502	to IQ4_NL from scratch: 40 billion weights through a sixteen-scale search,
503	`parallelFor` across every core. Measured 2026-09-19: **31 of 32 cores pinned
504	flat for the whole fit, 5731 CPU-seconds in the first 200 s, sys time 9.3 s**
505	— all arithmetic, no I/O. research/llm-vertical.md D21 prices the whole fit at ~8 minutes.
506	
507	Set it and staging is a disk read instead:
508	
509	    LLM_BANK_CACHE=models/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF/bank-cache
510	
511	With it, a 48-layer stage at 131k cells was **58.5 s total, MoE block 19.4 s**,
512	71.01 GB of weights + 5.09 GB of arenas. The cache directory is 26 GB and was
513	already complete for the shipped plan (48/48 files per family). It is keyed on
514	(tensor, shape, source type, target type, arm, version) and lives inside the
515	checkpoint's directory — it does **not** hash the source bytes.
516	
517	**The dense bank has no cache at all** (`llm/bank_q4.go`), so it re-fits every
518	start no matter what. Measured on the same 16 dense layers: banks off **8.6 s
519	wall / 46.9 CPU-s**, dense bank on **17.4 s / 134.6 CPU-s** — 2.9x the CPU.
520	That part is unavoidable today.
521	
522	**Why:** the CPU storm looks alarming and looks like inference gone wrong — it
523	is neither. It is startup-only weight preparation, which is why the served API
524	never shows it: the server pays the fit once ever and then holds the model
525	resident. During real inference the GPU sits at 98-99% and host cost is ~3 ms
526	of a ~31 ms token.
527	
528	**How to apply:** set `LLM_BANK_CACHE` in every `cmd/llm` invocation that also
529	sets `LLM_MOE_BANK`, and budget ~60 s of staging rather than ~8 minutes. See
530	[[llm-resident-run]] and [[strix-halo-bench-runs]].
531	---
532	name: llm-resident-run
533	description: The whole-model runs (`cmd/llm -resident`, `-graph`, `-gen`, `-ppl`, `cmd/serve -llm`, `TestGraphLogits`) stage 82-83 GB of qwen3.8-flash-next; what they cost in time and RAM, and why nothing else can run beside them.
534	metadata:
535	  type: project
536	---
537	
538	**Since L8a/L8b the dense banks are int8 rather than halves and residency is
539	81.89 GB with the head** (`-dense` 4.32 GB); `LLM_DENSE_FP16=1` puts every
540	block back on the old halves and restores the old sizes exactly, which is how
541	the two are compared. **A decode token is 31.7 ms and residency 79.85 GB as of
542	L8c-7 (2026-09-17)** with all five 4.5-bit families named in
543	`LLM_DENSE_BANK` — 40.5 ms at L8e, 33.3 at L8c-6, ~134 before L7d — so `-n 64`
544	is a ~2.0 s tail on top of staging. Without `LLM_DENSE_BANK` the run is still
545	L8a's int8 bank at 81.89 GB and 40.5 ms.
546	
547	**Do not schedule a whole-model run above ~2560 rows**: at 48 layers
548	`-graph -tokens 3072` (or `-ppl -ctx 4096`) **never returns** — it stalls
549	inside the driver's submit with one host thread at 100% and the GPU at 2-3%,
550	and the shim's 20 s fence timeout never fires, so it hangs indefinitely rather
551	than erroring. 2048 and 2560 are fine; the 4-layer prefix is fine at 4096.
552	This is a known open question in `research/llm-vertical.md`, not a mistake to re-discover.
553	
554	`go run ./cmd/llm -resident` (added 2026-09-16, research/llm-vertical.md L6a) stages every layer
555	of all five blocks: **84.20 GB of device buffers (82.40 since L8a), ~35 s wall
556	clock**, and it
557	ends with about 41 GB of MemAvailable left on this 117.7 GiB machine. Peak
558	host memory is separate — the dense blocks dequantise to f32 before packing,
559	and the 36 DeltaNet layers are 8.35 GB of transient floats at once — which is
560	why the tool stages dense first and the 77 GB expert bank last.
561	
562	**Why:** it is the only thing in the repo that takes most of the machine, so a
563	second GPU or large-allocation job started beside it will either fail to
564	allocate or perturb the timing it prints. `-bank N,N,...` restages just the
565	bank, which is the cheap way to vary residency; `-dense` is the 6.8 GB half
566	and runs in 8 s.
567	
568	`go run ./cmd/llm -graph` and `go test ./llm/ -run TestGraphLogits` (added
569	2026-09-16, research/llm-vertical.md L6b) are the same weight but **85.47 GB**, because they add
570	the 1.27 GB lm head; `-tokens 2048` adds another ~1.1 GB of arenas. Staging is
571	~35-40 s, so budget a 1800 s timeout. Both take a `-layers 4` / `GraphOpts{
572	Layers: 4}` prefix that is 7.4 GB and three seconds — use that while changing
573	anything about the order, and the full stage only for the gate.
574	
575	`go run ./cmd/llm -gen` (added 2026-09-16, research/llm-vertical.md L7c) is the same 85.47 GB
576	plus the KV cache, and it is the slow one: staging is ~35-50 s and generation
577	is **~40.5 ms a token** (see above), so `-n 64` is a ~2.6 s tail on top.
578	**Every committed decode CSV is `-prompt 'The capital of France is'`**; the
579	flag's default is the 81-token `graphDefaultPrompt`, on which the model emits
580	EOS at the first step and the decode row is meaningless. A 900 s timeout
581	covers `-n 64`; a two-minute one does not even cover the staging. `-layers 4`
582	is 7.4 GB, ~2 s to stage and ~18 ms a token, which is the right thing to use
583	for anything about the loop rather than about the rate.
584	
585	`go run ./cmd/llm -ppl` (added 2026-09-17, research/llm-vertical.md L8c-0) is the longest of
586	them: 81.89 GB, ~37 s of staging and then **3.3 s per 2048-token chunk for 145
587	chunks — 7m58s** over `wiki.test.raw`, so run it in the background and wait on
588	the log rather than holding a foreground timeout. `-chunks N` cuts it (4
589	chunks is ~15 s after staging) but **only screens for broken**: four chunks
590	read +0.32% against llama.cpp where the whole corpus reads −0.13%, sign and
591	all. `-layers 4` plus `-chunks 2` is the 8 GB plumbing check. The reference
592	side is `llama-perplexity -c 2048 -b 2048`, ~6.5 s a chunk, and it needs the
593	machine too — never both at once. **`LLM_DENSE_SIM=<plan>` forces the fp16
594	arm** (L8c-1), so a simulated run is the old 84 GB residency and ~6 s longer
595	to stage, and its tok/s means nothing — it grades accuracy only.
596	`LLM_DENSE_SIM_QUANT=imatrix` needs `models/…/imatrix_unsloth.gguf` (the
597	fetch script gets it; note the source's `_file` suffix) and adds ~10 s of
598	staging for the nineteen-rung scale search.
599	
600	**Since P4b/D20 (2026-09-19) a served-default run also stages the MoE bank
601	narrower, and it is not free at startup.** `LLM_MOE_BANK` (default off in
602	`cmd/llm`, set to `llm.ShippedMoEBank` by `cmd/serve -llm`) transcodes four
603	tensor families out of the checkpoint's bytes — 4.2 B weights of
604	`ffn_down_exps` plus 236 M of the shared expert — so **the MoE block stages
605	in ~52 s instead of ~25**, and a whole-model run is ~1m32s to first chunk
606	rather than ~40 s. Residency drops 77.41 -> 76.00 GB in that block (78.53 GB
607	whole-model with D19's dense bank). Budget the extra minute in every timeout;
608	`LLM_MOE_BANK=off` is the control.
609	
610	`go run ./cmd/serve -llm` (added 2026-09-17, research/llm-vertical.md L9a) is the same residency
611	held open: **33.5 s to stage at `-llm-ctx 4096`**, ~84 GB, and it then serves
612	until interrupted. A request is a prefill plus ~44 ms a token (22.7 tok/s
613	through the server on the L8 banks), so a 48-token answer is under a second.
614	Start it in the background, poll the log for `listening on`, and **kill it
615	with `pkill -f '[e]xe/serve'` when finished** — the bracket matters, because
616	`pkill -f 'exe/serve'` matches the shell running it and kills the session
617	instead (the same trap as [[watch-loops-must-not-match-themselves]]). It holds
618	the machine for as long as it runs. `-llm-layers 4` is the 7 GB, 3.5 s prefix
619	and is the right thing for anything about HTTP rather than about the text.
620	
621	**The access log prints no bodies by default** (`-log-bodies` turns them back
622	on): a chat server's bodies are conversations. The per-request `llm:` line is
623	separate and always printed — prompt tokens, how many were reused from the
624	last turn, and the two rates.
625	
626	**The model path must name a shard, not the directory.**
627	`models/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF/` now holds three checkpoints — the model, the
628	imatrix and the MTP head — so `gguf.OpenSet` refuses it as ambiguous and
629	`cmd/llm`'s own `-model` default no longer resolves. Pass
630	`models/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-UD-Q4_K_XL-00001-of-00004.gguf`,
631	which is what `cmd/serve` defaults to.
632	
633	**`-layers 24` is the end-to-end instrument when 48 will not fit.** With the
634	`ai` user service resident (~7 GB) this machine has ~80 GB MemAvailable
635	against a 48-layer `-graph`'s ~80 GB, which is too tight to schedule. A
636	24-layer `-graph` is **~40 GB, ~2 min to first number**, and it is a *real*
637	whole-graph measurement — all five blocks, the head, the host loop, the
638	per-block ms columns in the CSV — not a block bench. Its one distortion is
639	that the M-independent fixed costs (head 2.4 ms, `ple`, `move`, host) are 24%
640	of a step there against 13% at 48 layers, so any *ratio* read off it is
641	optimistic and the 48-layer number is owed (P5, 2026-09-19).
642	
643	**How to apply:** run them in the foreground with a long timeout and nothing
644	else on the GPU, the way [[strix-halo-bench-runs]] asks. `-resident`'s closing
645	measurement (layer 3's MoE block) is comparable to `-moe -tokens 512 -iters 10`
646	only at the same iteration count.
647	---
648	name: never-edit-source-during-a-sweep
649	description: "`go run` rebuilds on every invocation, so editing repo source while a multi-arm benchmark script is running kills every arm after the one already in flight."
650	metadata:
651	  type: feedback
652	---
653	
654	**2026-09-21.** A four-arm 48-layer depth sweep lost three of its four arms.
655	The script called `go run ./cmd/llm` once per arm; arm 1 had already built and
656	ran fine; while it ran I edited `shaders/shaders.go` to add a new `//go:embed`
657	for a `.spv` that did not exist yet, and arms 2-4 each died instantly with
658	
659	    shaders/shaders.go:2646:12: pattern llm_attn_expand.spv: no matching files found
660	
661	~25 minutes of measurement, and the failure was silent in the sweep's own log
662	until the end.
663	
664	[[strix-halo-bench-runs]] already says "edit *text* while it runs, nothing
665	else" — that rule is about CPU contention perturbing the numbers. This is a
666	second, harder reason: **a multi-arm script that invokes `go run` rebuilds the
667	tree at the start of every arm**, so the source it compiles is whatever the
668	tree holds *then*, not what it held at launch. Even an edit that compiles
669	would silently measure a different binary in later arms, which is worse than
670	a crash.
671	
672	**How to apply:** make the benchmark script `go build -o <scratchpad>/bench
673	./cmd/llm` **once at the top** and run that binary for every arm. Then the
674	tree is free to edit while it runs, and every arm is provably the same build.
675	Select arms with environment variables read at dispatch time (this is what
676	`LLM_ATTN_SPLITS` and `LLM_ATTN_CELL_SPLITS` are for), never by rebuilding.
677	---
678	name: auto-committer-owns-main
679	description: "An external process auto-commits the strix-halo-vulkan working tree to main every ~30-45 min with the message \"ai\", and other sessions edit the same tree concurrently, so `go build ./...` can fail on someone else's half-written file."
680	metadata: 
681	  node_type: memory
682	  type: project
683	  originSessionId: 8382387e-ec90-4d7d-8642-1d65b8bbd10a
684	  modified: 2026-09-17T23:25:30.192Z
685	---
686	
687	In `~/repos/strix-halo-vulkan` something outside the session commits the whole
688	working tree to `main` on a timer — the message is always `ai`, and the commits
689	land roughly every 30-45 minutes (observed 18:53, 19:37, 21:02, 21:36 on
690	2026-09-14). So a `git add -A && git commit` at the end of a session will often
691	print **"nothing to commit, working tree clean"** even though the work is
692	unsaved-looking: check `git show --stat HEAD` before concluding anything was
693	lost. There is an `origin` (github.com:theninj4/strix-halo-vulkan) but `main`
694	has **no upstream**, so nothing is pushed.
695	
696	**Other sessions edit this tree at the same time.** On 2026-09-18 a second
697	session was mid-refactor in `zimage/pipeline` and mid-write in `api/images.go`
698	while this one built `embed/`: `go build ./...` failed twice on *their*
699	undefined symbols (`p.latentH`, `formatSize`), minutes apart, and both cleared
700	on their own. Check `git status --short` and file mtimes before believing a
701	build break is yours, and build the packages you touched
702	(`go build ./embed/ ./api/ …`) rather than `./...` while it lasts.
703	
704	**Why:** the commit log is therefore not the project's narrative — `TODO.md`
705	is, and every session appends a handoff to it. That is why the repo's own docs
706	say to read `TODO.md`/the current vertical file first.
707	
708	**How to apply:** don't branch before committing here (the whole history is
709	direct-to-main), don't amend the `ai` commits to "improve" them, and put the
710	session's story in `TODO.md` rather than in a commit message. Edit files with
711	targeted replacements rather than whole-file rewrites when another session may
712	be in the same file, and never "fix" a symbol that belongs to their in-flight
713	work. See [[strix-halo-bench-runs]] and [[phase-2-pivot-to-pipeline]] for what
714	the docs expect a session to record.

---
name: long-context-prefill-128k
description: "Prefill against depth out to 128k after P14 (2026-09-22): 826 tok/s at ubatch 2048 and 946 at 8192, the four changes, the four measured refusals, and the fast 4-layer probe."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 80f71c47-a621-4724-a77a-e285f8d84b61
  modified: 2026-09-22T11:38:44.739Z
---

**128 000 cells prefills at 826.0 tok/s at ubatch 2048 and 946.1 at
8192 — `GOALS.md`'s 900 is met.** P13 left it at 563.6. 48 layers, shipped banks,
`wiki.test.raw`, one sequence walked forward, `-tg 8 -ctx 139000`. Write-up
`research/p14-prefill-at-depth.md`.

| depth | P13 pp | P14 pp | | decode |
|------:|-------:|-------:|----:|-------:|
| 0 | 1129.3 | 1154.2 | 1.02x | 29.31 |
| 32 000 | 825.8 | 915.6 | 1.11x | 25.80 |
| 64 000 | 719.6 | 892.1 | 1.24x | 24.46 |
| 96 000 | 607.9 | 832.3 | 1.37x | 22.80 |
| **128 000** | **563.6** | **826.0** | **1.47x** | 22.18 |

Falloff from depth zero **0.50x → 0.72x**. Against the ubatch at 128 000 alone
(two runs each): 826.0 at 2048, 886.1 at 4096 (the shipped
`-llm-batch`), **946.1 at 8192** — P12's trade at depth, so 8192 is a
batch summariser's setting. **Decode is the control and did not move.**

**Four changes.**

1. **The selection runs over block scores, not the expanded per-cell tensor**
   (`llm_attn_selblk.comp`). All `ratio` cells of a pooled block carry one score,
   so a weighted select over `nKV/ratio` entries is the same threshold, ties and
   bitmask. `attn.select` 0.281 → **0.020** (13.8x), `attn.expand` deleted, and
   **1.14 GB of arena** freed at ubatch 2048. Bit-identical, gated by
   `TestAttnGPUSelectBlocksIsTheCellSelect` over four chunk schedules.
2. **The attention runs over a per-cell gather** (`llm_attn_gather.comp` +
   `llm_attn_wmma.comp -DGATHER`). Per query tile, the union of its rows'
   selections compacted ascending, with the causal test folded into a per-row
   mask over the gathered positions. `attn.attn` 1.024 → **0.454** (2.15x on the
   4-layer probe; 0.566 → 0.303 at 48 layers). **The value plane had to become
   cell-major first** — a selected run is `ratio` consecutive cells, one
   128-byte line, where transposed it was four halves out of sixteen rows. That
   costs the block kernel ~7% and decode nothing.
3. **The indexer's score on the matrix cores** (`llm_attn_score_wmma.comp`). It
   is a GEMM per indexer head with a rectifier: 0.077 → **0.034**. Chunk-invariant
   (a matrix product's rows are independent), and *nearer* llama.cpp's selection
   than the scalar kernel (9760 vs 9762 of 6 298 621).
4. **`checkBufferRange`** — see [[a-benchmark-that-gets-faster]].

**The gather is the first kernel here that is not chunk-invariant and cannot be
made so.** Its list is the union of a query tile's sixteen rows, so a chunk
ending inside the tile gathers a different list and the online softmax folds the
same terms in a different order. It is off under `Graph.PinSchedule` with the
other reassociating kernels, and the chunk-equality gates pin it (`SetGather`).
A prompt prefilled twice at the same ubatch is still bit-identical; only changing
the ubatch moves the last places. Gates: `TestAttnGPUGatherSelectsTheSameCells`
(exact on the set), `TestAttnGPUGatherIsTheBlockKernel` (4.1e-06 rms against
9.9e-04 from llama.cpp), `TestAttnGPUGatherRungsAgree`,
`TestAttnGPUGatherIsDispatched`.

**The union is the number that prices all of this, and P13's estimate of it was
wrong.** `AttnGPU.SelUnion` measures it: at 128 000 cells a 16-row tile reads
**15 145** cells where its rows' union is **7 049** and one row selects 2 051.
The gather is therefore 2.15x, not the 3.3x P13 projected, and the 3.4x between
the union and one row is the floor a 16-row fragment cannot reach.

**What the gathered kernel is bound by, by elimination** — four arms, all
1.00x-ish, in [[prefill-rates]]: not the matrix cores (doubling their work costs
2.7%), not the barriers, not the gather's own traffic (sharing it across two
heads buys 4%). It is the LDS round-trip for the fragments and the per-head
softmax scaffolding, both linear in the union.

**The fast loop is still `-depth ... -layers 4`, 40 seconds an arm** — and it
**overstates** `attn.attn` because its one attention layer is denser than the
48-layer mean (19.0% live at bm16/bn16 against 11.7%). Ratios reproduce;
absolutes do not.

    /tmp/pp -model $M -depth -depths 0,64000,128000 -pp 2048 -tg 4 -ctx 136000 -layers 4

**Control arms**: `LLM_ATTN_GATHER=0`, `LLM_ATTN_GATHER_KERNEL=qt1_kt1|qt1_kt4`,
`LLM_ATTN_GATHER_GRP`, `LLM_ATTN_GATHER_HEADS`, `LLM_ATTN_EXPAND_CELLS=1` (also
what `Cells()` needs), `LLM_ATTN_SCORE=scalar`.

**The whole-model check.** Three of the four changes claim bit-exactness, and
`TestGraphLogits` confirms all three at once: its diagnostics come back
byte-identical to the base (`maxAbs 2.507e+00 at 141557`, `rms 5.148e-01`, the
same top ten) through all 48 layers. Its *failure* is the pre-existing one — see
[[llm-test-suite-gotchas]], and note that a relative `LLM_BANK_CACHE` there
writes 23 GB into `llm/models`, which this session walked into.

See [[prefill-rates]], [[context-depth-rates]], [[a-benchmark-that-gets-faster]],
[[llm-bench-needs-bank-cache]], [[never-edit-source-during-a-sweep]],
[[strix-halo-bench-runs]], [[graphstats-kinds-aliases]].
---
name: decode-at-depth-after-p15
description: "Decode rates against context depth after P16 (2026-09-22): 34.4 tok/s at depth zero, 31.5 at 128k, the wide-batch cost that was a padding bug, the four depth terms and the control knobs."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: dedbcc64-a855-44f2-a0fa-3d37d0946061
  modified: 2026-09-22T15:25:15.756Z
---

**Quote this table for decode — P16's (2026-09-22), not P15's.** 48 layers,
shipped banks, `-pp 2048 -tg 16 -ctx 139000`, `wiki.test.raw`, two passes to
0.3%, write-up `research/p16-decode-arena-width.md`.

| depth | pp tok/s | tg tok/s | P15 tg |
|------:|---------:|---------:|-------:|
| 0 | 1155.8 | **34.39** | 29.73 |
| 8 000 | 973.9 | 33.54 | 28.78 |
| 32 000 | 919.7 | 33.20 | 28.72 |
| 64 000 | 896.3 | 32.41 | 28.14 |
| 128 000 | 834.4 | **31.53** | 27.20 |

At ubatch 4096 (`-ctx 141000`, three depths — five overflow the descriptor):
0 → 1292.5 / 33.01, 64k → 979.4 / 33.00, **128k → 904.6 / 31.63**.

**P16's lesson, which generalises: a knob that costs decode is found by a
per-label diff between the two arms, not by theorising.** The wide-arena cost
was blamed on memory residency for two passes (P12-7, P15); `-depth -ubatch`
(arena rows separate from `-pp`) showed it followed the arena, and the label
diff put all of it on `move`, `dn.qkv`, `attn.qkv` in one look — the input
ports padded a one-row decode step with zeros to the whole arena. A padding
that is *correct* and slow is invisible to every tolerance test; it is gated
now by `TestInPortPadsTheRunNotTheArena`. Also P16: `hc.cn` runs a workgroup a
(token, stream) at ≤ 64 rows (`LLM_HC_CN_SPLIT_ROWS`, 0 = P11's grid), and
`attn.select`'s emit walks blocks (68 → 55 µs at 128k); its passes are neither
load-latency- nor atomic-contention-bound (both measured, 0.96x and 0.69x).

**The P15 section below still stands for what it explains** (the four depth
terms), with P16's rates on top.

**A deep decode step is four terms and nothing else.** Every other kernel in
the model is flat in depth — `moe.up` 5.44 ms a token at both ends, `dn.qkv`
4.39, `hc.cn` 2.33. At 128 000 cells, base → final:

- `attn.attn.split` 4.109 → **1.571** (the gather+split, P15-3)
- host `gather`, i.e. `PLERows` 5.175 → **1.263** (P15-1)
- `attn.score` 2.533 → **0.995** (the stripe at 64, P15-2)
- `attn.select` 0.862 → **0.862** — untouched, and now the largest
  depth-scaling term left on the device

**The largest one was on the host.** `PLERows(cfg, g.ids)` hashed the whole
sequence every token and sliced off the tail — 8.2 MB allocated and 2.05 M rows
per step at 128k to use sixteen. `PLERowsFrom` is the tail-only form and is
exact by construction. The `-depth` bench had been printing that as a `gather`
line growing 3.1% → 11.7% with depth for as long as it has existed. **Read the
host lines of the profile, not only the kernel ones.**

**The control knobs**, all env, all on `cmd/llm -depth`:

    LLM_ATTN_GATHER=0            # P8's block split, which is what decode had
    LLM_ATTN_GATHER_MIN=<cells>  # the depth the gathered arm turns on at
    LLM_ATTN_CELL_SPLITS=16      # P9's stripe count, shipped at 64
    LLM_ARENA_UNCACHED=1         # the arena memory type
    LLM_NO_PRERECORD=1           # re-record every decode step

**The gates after touching any of this** (plus P7-P10's, in
[[context-depth-rates]]):

    go test ./llm/ -run TestPLERowsFromIsTheTail                   # exact
    go test ./llm/ -run TestAttnGPUGatherSplitIsTheGather          # tolerance
    go test ./llm/ -run TestPrerecordedDecodeCrossesTheGatherBound # the epoch

**Two traps this pass walked into, both worth remembering.** A split-kernel
test that uploads the whole fixture at once passes with 0.000e+00 on every arm,
because `attnSplits` refuses any batch wider than `attnSplitMaxRows` — a split
that never engaged looks exactly like a perfect one, so assert on a zero. And
the obvious test for the prerecord epoch — diff the logits across the bound
with the replay on and off — **cannot fail**, because below the selection's
2051-cell width the gathered and block kernels are bit-identical; assert the
mechanism (`preEpoch` against the depth) instead.

**How to apply:** needs `LLM_BANK_CACHE` — see [[llm-bench-needs-bank-cache]],
[[strix-halo-bench-runs]], [[never-edit-source-during-a-sweep]] and
[[llm-resident-run]]. The fast loop is `-depths 128000 -pp 2048 -tg 8 -layers 4`,
~60 s an arm, and it reproduces the `attn.attn` ratios to the microsecond.

name: context-depth-rates
description: "Decode rates against context depth after P7/P8/P9/P10, what each removed, and the gates to run after touching attention; the gather is the last big item. Prefill and 128k are superseded by P13 (long-context-prefill-128k)."
metadata:
  type: project
---

**The depth regression is closed, in four stages, all 2026-09-21.** Decode at
64 000 cells went **4.05 → 15.91 → 26.76 → 27.69 tok/s** and the falloff from
depth zero **0.14x → 0.48x → 0.76x → 0.79x**. Write-ups:
`research/p7-context-depth.md`, `research/p8-decode-attention-split.md`
(which covers P8, P9 and P10). CSVs `results/p7_depth_*`,
`results/p10_depth_{base,p89,p8910}[_run2].csv`.

48 layers, shipped banks, `-pp 512 -tg 64`, ctx 66 880, `wiki.test.raw`,
three arms interleaved, two passes each (means):

| depth | base (P7) | +P8+P9 | +P8+P9+P10 | pp |
|------:|----------:|-------:|-----------:|---:|
| 0 | 33.16 | 35.06 | **35.08** | 691 |
| 8 000 | 22.74 | 32.18 | **32.40** | 579 |
| 16 000 | 20.53 | 31.12 | **31.35** | 558 |
| 32 000 | 18.06 | 29.14 | **29.68** | 532 |
| 64 000 | 15.91 | 26.76 | **27.69** | 440 |

A decode step at 64k: **62.9 → 36.1 ms**. The attention block across twelve
layers: **30.80 → 7.28 ms** a token (4.23x).

**What each stage removed.**

1. **P7 — `nKV` is the allocated cache, not the context.** Three kernels
   looped on it, paid in full *at depth zero*; and QSA was a mask and never a
   skip. See its own write-up — both are easy to reintroduce.
2. **P8/P9/P10 — at decode the kernels are single waves that all fit at
   once.** See [[decode-is-latency-not-bandwidth]]; this is the reusable one.
   P8 splits the attention's key axis 16 ways (strided, constant count,
   folded by `llm_attn_combine.comp`); P9 splits the indexer's score from its
   cell expansion so both can stripe; P10 widens the *selection* from four
   waves to sixteen, because a radix select is a reduction and cannot be
   striped at all — the only parallelism left is waves on its one CU.

**Prefill is untouched by P8/P9 and that is the control** — 692.6 → 690.5 at
depth 0 and 438.8 → 441.9 at 64 000, inside the noise. Prefill's 0.63x
falloff is the quadratic term any dense attention has; llama.cpp has it too.

**The gates after touching any of this**:

    go test ./llm/ -run TestAttnGPUCacheSizeDoesNotChangeTheAnswer   # P7
    go test ./llm/ -run TestAttnGPUSplitMatchesUnsplit               # P8
    go test ./llm/ -run TestAttnGPUCellStripeDoesNotChangeTheAnswer  # P9, exact
    go test ./llm/ -run TestAttnGPUSelectWidthDoesNotChangeTheAnswer # P10, exact
    go test ./llm/ -run TestGraphIsAChunkSplit                       # the graph

`LLM_ATTN_SPLITS=1`, `LLM_ATTN_CELL_SPLITS=1` and `LLM_ATTN_SELECT_WG=256`
are the control arms.
**P8 is not bit-identical** and is covered by `PinSchedule` with the other
five reassociating decode kernels; P9 **is** bit-identical.

**Superseded for prefill by P13 and then P14 (both 2026-09-22)** — 128k completes, and the
attention rung at depth is now `qt1_kt1`: see [[long-context-prefill-128k]]
for the rates out to 128 000 cells — 128k prefills past 900 tok/s now and the
attention rung at depth is the **gathered** kernel, not a block one. The decode
table below stands, and decode is P14's control: it did not move.

**Superseded for decode by P15 (2026-09-22)** — see
[[decode-at-depth-after-p15]] for the table that stands now: decode at 128k is
**27.20 tok/s** and the falloff **0.91x**, and the three things that got it
there were a *host* function, a stripe count and the gather+split composition.
The paragraph below is what P10 left and is kept for the P7-P10 attribution.

**Still open as of P10**: **the gather** is now the only large item — of the 5.9 ms a
decode step still gains between depth 0 and 64k, the split attention is 3.0,
because the split shortened the walk sixteenfold without stopping it being a
walk over every key block. More slices is **not** the answer and that is
measured: 0.318 / 0.288 / 0.291 / 0.283 ms at 8 / 16 / 32 / 64 slices while
the combine climbs 0.004 / 0.006 / 0.010 / 0.018. **128 000 still does not
complete**
— the fill dies at ~115k in P0's timestamp pathology reached by depth; the
untried route is making `DispatchMultiMarked`'s per-dispatch marks optional.

**How to apply:** quote this table, not P7's and not the 2026-09-19 one; never
compare two depth-0 rates measured at different `-ctx`. Needs
`LLM_BANK_CACHE` — see [[llm-bench-needs-bank-cache]],
[[strix-halo-bench-runs]] and [[never-edit-source-during-a-sweep]].

name: prefill-rates
description: "Prompt-processing rates after P12 (2026-09-21), the ubatch curve and the decode cost that comes with it, what the MoE prefill GEMM is bound by, and the four prefill ideas that are measured dead."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: d77f87a5-b722-4ac5-aaa9-d322f713f1da
  modified: 2026-09-21T22:34:23.069Z
---

**Prefill does not plateau where llama.cpp's does, so the ubatch is a real
knob — but widening it is a trade, not a free win.** 48 layers, shipped banks,
two runs each (`results/p12_pp_*.csv`, write-ups `research/p11-prefill.md` and
`research/p12-prefill-round-two.md`):

**Superseded at depth by P14 (2026-09-22)** — see [[long-context-prefill-128k]]
for the rates against context depth, which are no longer these. The depth-zero
ladder below stands.

| ubatch | P11 | P12 | vs llama.cpp |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 512 | 681.7 | 683.3 | 1.75x |
| 2048 | 1191.8 | **1207.7** | 3.08x |
| 4096 | 1340.7 | 1363.5 | 3.48x |
| 8192 | 1372.2 | **1403.9** | **3.59x** |

Against **context depth** at ubatch 2048: 1154.6 / 968.1 / 894.3 / 805.7 /
**667.7** tok/s at 0 / 8k / 16k / 32k / 64k. Arms are reproducible to
0.1-0.5%, so a 1.2% difference is real; quote means of two passes.

**`-llm-batch` defaults to 4096 and, since P16 (2026-09-22), a wider batch
costs memory and nothing else.** P12-7 measured 4096 costing 8% of decode
through the server and P15 11-22% at depth; **that was a bug** — the DeltaNet
and attention input ports zero-padded a decode step out to the whole arena.
Fixed, through the server (four ~4k prompts, 256 generated, two passes to 0.1%):

| batch | prefill | decode |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 2048 | 1052.2 | 34.19 |
| 4096 | 1198.5 | 34.20 |
| 8192 | 1232.5 | 34.16 |

8192 only helps prompts > 4096 tokens, holds ~3 GB more, and lowers the
`maxStorageBufferRange` context cap. See [[decode-at-depth-after-p15]].

**The MoE prefill GEMM is bound by its per-tile slab unpack, not by rows.**
Measured four ways in P11 (row padding 1.90x → 1.19x is worth *nothing*; a
per-fragment bound, three sub-lists, and BM 128 all lose). So the way to speed
`moe.up` up is fewer tiles at the same block width = fewer experts touched = a
bigger ubatch. P12 adds the floor: **gutting the whole Q4_K scale path is only
1.21x**, and what remains after the loads are collected — an int→float
convert, an FMA and an f16 convert per weight — has **no bit-exact cheaper
form** (packed fp16 costs ~13 bits of mantissa; `v_cvt_pkrtz` rounds toward
zero). At 21.1 TFLOP/s and 61 GB/s of bank it is neither matrix-core- nor
bandwidth-bound.

**What is measured dead (do not re-attempt without new information):**

- **Four arms on the gathered attention kernel, P14 (2026-09-22)**, and together
  they say what it is bound by. *Doubling the QK matrix work costs 2.7%*, so the
  matrix cores are ~5% of it. A subgroup staging barrier instead of a workgroup
  one is **1.00x**; staging two head-dim groups a barrier is **1.00x** and four
  is **0.75x**; putting two query heads in one workgroup so they share the staged
  key and value — which halves both the gather's global reads and its LDS writes
  — is **1.04x**, and four is **0.75x**. So it is not the matrix cores, not the
  barriers, not the gather's traffic and not occupancy-to-spare: what is left is
  the **LDS round-trip for the fragments and the per-head softmax scaffolding**,
  both of which scale with the union, which is why the kernel's cost is linear in
  the cells it visits. The 0.75x arms are LDS crowding out waves.
  `LLM_ATTN_GATHER_GRP` and `LLM_ATTN_GATHER_HEADS` are the ladders, both at 1.

- **Compacting the live key blocks into a per-query-tile list is 1.00x at
  every depth** (P13, 2026-09-22) — it deletes 83% of the axis walk at 128k
  and `attn.attn` does not move. Third instance of the same rule, which is now
  the engine's and not any kernel's: *latency and redundant reads that matter
  at decode do not matter at prefill, because prefill has occupancy* — 3072
  single-wave workgroups against a decode step's 24. See
  [[long-context-prefill-128k]].

- **`hc.cn`'s 256-way reduction tree costs nothing** — deleting it outright is
  5331.5 µs against 5325.8. The non-bit-exact subgroup rewrite P11 queued
  would have bought zero.
- **`hc.cn`'s per-token gamma read costs nothing** — replacing it with a
  constant is 5332.9 µs. It is 40 KB and the MALL serves it. Its 57% of copy
  bandwidth is now *unexplained and out of hypotheses*.
- **Hoisting the attention block skip out of the loop is 1.00x at every
  depth.** At 64k a query tile skips ~1480 blocks, each on a dependent global
  read; voting on the whole key range up front with a subgroup ballot buys
  nothing, because **a prefill dispatches 3072 single-wave workgroups where a
  decode step dispatches 24** — latency that matters at decode does not matter
  at prefill, because prefill has occupancy. The exact converse of P8. **Still
  live for decode**, where it was deliberately never built.
- **The selection mask loop is 3.5-8%** of the attention kernel, not the rest
  of the depth gap.

**At depth the fast loop is `-depth -layers 4`, 40 seconds an arm**
([[long-context-prefill-128k]]) — `-attn` runs at `past = 0` and never
reaches depth's regime.

**`cmd/llm -attn` is the fast loop for attention at depth zero and it is 1.9 seconds** (two
layers, real routing, real selection, per-label µs a layer) — use it, not the
7-minute `-graph` ladder. It tops out near 16 384 tokens (32 768 in one batch
trips P0's watchdog) and runs at `past = 0`, so it reaches the selection's
regime but **not depth's**; only `-depth` does. `cmd/llm -moe` is the MoE's
equivalent at 228 ms to stage. See [[context-depth-rates]] for decode,
[[llm-bench-needs-bank-cache]], [[never-edit-source-during-a-sweep]],
[[llm-test-suite-gotchas]].
