name: decode-is-latency-not-bandwidth
description: "At decode this model's per-head GPU kernels are single waves that all fit on the device at once, so a dispatch costs one wave's serial walk — not its traffic and not its total work."
metadata:
  type: project
---

**P8, 2026-09-21.** The probe that settles it: cutting the attention grid from
24 workgroups to 2 — a twelfth of the work *and* a twelfth of the traffic —
measured **1.00x at every depth** (0, 16 384 and 65 536 cells, three decimal
places).

The reason is structural and applies well beyond attention. A decode step is
**one token**, so any kernel gridded on (query blocks, heads) or on (tokens,
…) dispatches a handful of workgroups; `local_size_x = WAVE` makes each one a
single wave; and this device has **40 compute units**. Everything launches at
once, nothing queues, and the dispatch's wall clock is the *longest single
wave's serial loop*. With one wave per CU there is nothing to hide a
`coopMatLoad`'s latency behind, which is why the measured rate was ~7 GB/s
where prefill on the same kernel achieves hundreds.

So at decode:

- **Adding parallelism across heads buys nothing** — they already run
  concurrently.
- **Removing redundant traffic buys nothing** — the redundant readers were
  never queued behind each other. (12 query heads share each of the 2 KV
  planes here and each re-reads it in full; deleting that is free and worth
  nothing.)
- **Only shortening the per-workgroup loop helps**, by splitting the reduction
  axis across more workgroups, or by making the loop's iterations fewer.

Two kernels were fixed this way and a third is open — see
[[context-depth-rates]] for the numbers and `research/p8-decode-attention-split.md`.
`llm_attn_select.comp` is still one workgroup a token.

**How to apply:** before optimising any decode kernel in this repo, check its
grid at `rows == 1` first. If it is tens of workgroups, the question is the
length of one wave's loop and *not* the bytes it moves — and the cheap probe
is to cut the grid and see whether the time moves at all. Do not reason from
bandwidth at decode; that reasoning is right at prefill and wrong here.

**A prefill-shaped grid breaks this rule silently** (P16, 2026-09-22): P11
merged `hc.cn` to one workgroup a token for prefill bandwidth, which at decode
made it one workgroup walking four streams — 25 µs where a stream a workgroup
is 7. When a kernel is re-gridded for prefill, re-time it at `rows == 1`.

---
name: strix-halo-bench-runs
description: "How the strix-halo-vulkan benchmark suite is run and how long each family takes, plus the run-quality conventions the repo's docs expect."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 6c27486f-644d-4f43-a0b0-6ebe2136679b
  modified: 2026-09-18T12:55:03.680Z
---

`go run ./cmd/bench -blocks 32,64,128,256,512,1024 <family>` — the non-default
block list is what every committed `results/*.csv` was measured with, so keep
it if rows are to stay comparable. `go generate ./...` first if any `.comp`
changed (`*.spv` is gitignored). As of 2026-09-13 the `moe` family is ~9
minutes / 896 rows; it prints its summary tables only at the end, so there is
no progress output to poll — run it in the foreground with a long timeout.
The `bank` family (added 2026-09-15, research/llm-vertical.md L0a) is the odd one out: its 72
timed cells are seconds, but `go run ./cmd/bench -bankgib 64 -bankreadmib 1024
bank` first allocates 64 GiB in 19 buffers and writes one word per 4 KB page,
which is most of its ~3-minute wall clock. Check `free -g` has the headroom
before starting it.

**A whole-model tok/s number is only comparable against a control run the
same hour** (P1c, 2026-09-18): with an identical binary the decode step
measured 30.51 ms one day and 39.20 the next — every *dense-bank* kernel
1.6-1.9x slower (dn.qkv 115→206 us, head 1964→3531) while every MoE
expert-bank rung was unchanged. Suspected GTT page fragmentation of the
float-staged dense banks (32-day uptime, swap 100% full); unprovable without
root. **And a difference below ~0.5 tok/s needs interleaved A/B/A/B pairs, not one
pair** (P3, 2026-09-18): three pairs of the same two banks gave −0.06, +0.14
and +0.05 tok/s, so either single pair would have reported a signed number
where the truth was a within-arm spread of 0.31 against a real difference of
~0.04. Quote the means and the within-arm spread, not one delta.

So when measuring a decode/prefill change, rebuild yesterday's code in
a worktree (`.spv` are gitignored — regenerate or copy them) and run both
binaries back to back; never quote a delta against a prior day's CSV. Also:
run 1 of a freshly staged graph diverges from runs 2+ at ~1.6e-5 in the
logits (research/p1c-prerecorded-decode.md finding 4) — warm the graph once
before any bitwise comparison.

One-token `-ladder` runs of `cmd/llm` (moe/dn/attn/hc) must defeat the 32 MiB
MALL or every rate is an L3 number: stage many layers and use `-iters 1`
(e.g. `-moe -tokens 1 -ladder -layers 16 -iters 1`, P1b 2026-09-18 —
`ProfileSweep` walks a dispatch kind across layers, so each timing reads a
cold bank). The screen: any CSV row whose gbps exceeds 242 was not measuring
DRAM. The default two-layer, 20-iter form re-reads a ~32 MB working set from
the MALL.

**`go generate` after a `.comp` edit is load-bearing, and skipping it fails
*silently and flatteringly*.** `.spv` is gitignored and embedded into the Go
binary, so an edited shader that was not regenerated runs the **previous**
kernel — and a hand-compile to `/tmp` to check syntax is not the same thing.
On 2026-09-19 (P5b) that produced a whole round of measurements that read as a
2x speed-up and a full set of green tests, because the old kernel was doing
half the work on the new grid. Regenerate just the families touched
(`grep "go:generate" shaders/shaders.go | grep <file>.comp | sed 's|^//go:generate ||'`
into a loop) and check the `.spv` mtime before believing any number.

**Why:** the repo's TODO.md handoffs report a reproducibility figure for every
session (two runs of the family, median ratio and p10-p90 over common rows),
so a session that measures anything is expected to run its family twice and
quote the agreement.

**How to apply:** budget ~20 minutes for two `moe` runs, save each log and CSV
to the scratchpad so run N-1 survives for the comparison, and check nothing
else is using the GPU (`/sys/class/drm/card1/device/gpu_busy_percent`) before
starting. **"Nothing else" includes your own `go build` and `go test`** — a
whole-model decode step is ~3 ms of host work in ~28, and compiling beside a
`-gen` run cost one control pass 1.6 tok/s of 35 (P4c, 2026-09-19), which is
four times the difference such a run is usually measuring. Start the
measurement detached (`setsid nohup … &`, or the foreground loop will kill it
when the tool call times out) and edit *text* while it runs, nothing else. Do not poll with `pgrep -f` — see
[[watch-loops-must-not-match-themselves]].
---
name: llm-bench-needs-bank-cache
description: "Benchmarking cmd/llm on the shipped banks needs LLM_BANK_CACHE set by hand, or every process start re-fits the MoE bank for eight minutes on all 32 cores."
metadata:
  type: project
---

**`cmd/serve` sets `LLM_BANK_CACHE`; `cmd/llm` never does** (the comment at
`cmd/serve/main.go:177` says so outright). So a `cmd/llm` run launched with
`LLM_MOE_BANK` at the shipped plan but no cache path re-fits `ffn_down_exps`
to IQ4_NL from scratch: 40 billion weights through a sixteen-scale search,
`parallelFor` across every core. Measured 2026-09-19: **31 of 32 cores pinned
flat for the whole fit, 5731 CPU-seconds in the first 200 s, sys time 9.3 s**
— all arithmetic, no I/O. research/llm-vertical.md D21 prices the whole fit at ~8 minutes.

Set it and staging is a disk read instead:

    LLM_BANK_CACHE=models/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF/bank-cache

With it, a 48-layer stage at 131k cells was **58.5 s total, MoE block 19.4 s**,
71.01 GB of weights + 5.09 GB of arenas. The cache directory is 26 GB and was
already complete for the shipped plan (48/48 files per family). It is keyed on
(tensor, shape, source type, target type, arm, version) and lives inside the
checkpoint's directory — it does **not** hash the source bytes.

**The dense bank has no cache at all** (`llm/bank_q4.go`), so it re-fits every
start no matter what. Measured on the same 16 dense layers: banks off **8.6 s
wall / 46.9 CPU-s**, dense bank on **17.4 s / 134.6 CPU-s** — 2.9x the CPU.
That part is unavoidable today.

**Why:** the CPU storm looks alarming and looks like inference gone wrong — it
is neither. It is startup-only weight preparation, which is why the served API
never shows it: the server pays the fit once ever and then holds the model
resident. During real inference the GPU sits at 98-99% and host cost is ~3 ms
of a ~31 ms token.

**How to apply:** set `LLM_BANK_CACHE` in every `cmd/llm` invocation that also
sets `LLM_MOE_BANK`, and budget ~60 s of staging rather than ~8 minutes. See
[[llm-resident-run]] and [[strix-halo-bench-runs]].
---
name: llm-resident-run
description: The whole-model runs (`cmd/llm -resident`, `-graph`, `-gen`, `-ppl`, `cmd/serve -llm`, `TestGraphLogits`) stage 82-83 GB of qwen3.8-flash-next; what they cost in time and RAM, and why nothing else can run beside them.
metadata:
  type: project
---

**Since L8a/L8b the dense banks are int8 rather than halves and residency is
81.89 GB with the head** (`-dense` 4.32 GB); `LLM_DENSE_FP16=1` puts every
block back on the old halves and restores the old sizes exactly, which is how
the two are compared. **A decode token is 31.7 ms and residency 79.85 GB as of
L8c-7 (2026-09-17)** with all five 4.5-bit families named in
`LLM_DENSE_BANK` — 40.5 ms at L8e, 33.3 at L8c-6, ~134 before L7d — so `-n 64`
is a ~2.0 s tail on top of staging. Without `LLM_DENSE_BANK` the run is still
L8a's int8 bank at 81.89 GB and 40.5 ms.

**Do not schedule a whole-model run above ~2560 rows**: at 48 layers
`-graph -tokens 3072` (or `-ppl -ctx 4096`) **never returns** — it stalls
inside the driver's submit with one host thread at 100% and the GPU at 2-3%,
and the shim's 20 s fence timeout never fires, so it hangs indefinitely rather
than erroring. 2048 and 2560 are fine; the 4-layer prefix is fine at 4096.
This is a known open question in `research/llm-vertical.md`, not a mistake to re-discover.

`go run ./cmd/llm -resident` (added 2026-09-16, research/llm-vertical.md L6a) stages every layer
of all five blocks: **84.20 GB of device buffers (82.40 since L8a), ~35 s wall
clock**, and it
ends with about 41 GB of MemAvailable left on this 117.7 GiB machine. Peak
host memory is separate — the dense blocks dequantise to f32 before packing,
and the 36 DeltaNet layers are 8.35 GB of transient floats at once — which is
why the tool stages dense first and the 77 GB expert bank last.

**Why:** it is the only thing in the repo that takes most of the machine, so a
second GPU or large-allocation job started beside it will either fail to
allocate or perturb the timing it prints. `-bank N,N,...` restages just the
bank, which is the cheap way to vary residency; `-dense` is the 6.8 GB half
and runs in 8 s.

`go run ./cmd/llm -graph` and `go test ./llm/ -run TestGraphLogits` (added
2026-09-16, research/llm-vertical.md L6b) are the same weight but **85.47 GB**, because they add
the 1.27 GB lm head; `-tokens 2048` adds another ~1.1 GB of arenas. Staging is
~35-40 s, so budget a 1800 s timeout. Both take a `-layers 4` / `GraphOpts{
Layers: 4}` prefix that is 7.4 GB and three seconds — use that while changing
anything about the order, and the full stage only for the gate.

`go run ./cmd/llm -gen` (added 2026-09-16, research/llm-vertical.md L7c) is the same 85.47 GB
plus the KV cache, and it is the slow one: staging is ~35-50 s and generation
is **~40.5 ms a token** (see above), so `-n 64` is a ~2.6 s tail on top.
**Every committed decode CSV is `-prompt 'The capital of France is'`**; the
flag's default is the 81-token `graphDefaultPrompt`, on which the model emits
EOS at the first step and the decode row is meaningless. A 900 s timeout
covers `-n 64`; a two-minute one does not even cover the staging. `-layers 4`
is 7.4 GB, ~2 s to stage and ~18 ms a token, which is the right thing to use
for anything about the loop rather than about the rate.

`go run ./cmd/llm -ppl` (added 2026-09-17, research/llm-vertical.md L8c-0) is the longest of
them: 81.89 GB, ~37 s of staging and then **3.3 s per 2048-token chunk for 145
chunks — 7m58s** over `wiki.test.raw`, so run it in the background and wait on
the log rather than holding a foreground timeout. `-chunks N` cuts it (4
chunks is ~15 s after staging) but **only screens for broken**: four chunks
read +0.32% against llama.cpp where the whole corpus reads −0.13%, sign and
all. `-layers 4` plus `-chunks 2` is the 8 GB plumbing check. The reference
side is `llama-perplexity -c 2048 -b 2048`, ~6.5 s a chunk, and it needs the
machine too — never both at once. **`LLM_DENSE_SIM=<plan>` forces the fp16
arm** (L8c-1), so a simulated run is the old 84 GB residency and ~6 s longer
to stage, and its tok/s means nothing — it grades accuracy only.
`LLM_DENSE_SIM_QUANT=imatrix` needs `models/…/imatrix_unsloth.gguf` (the
fetch script gets it; note the source's `_file` suffix) and adds ~10 s of
staging for the nineteen-rung scale search.

**Since P4b/D20 (2026-09-19) a served-default run also stages the MoE bank
narrower, and it is not free at startup.** `LLM_MOE_BANK` (default off in
`cmd/llm`, set to `llm.ShippedMoEBank` by `cmd/serve -llm`) transcodes four
tensor families out of the checkpoint's bytes — 4.2 B weights of
`ffn_down_exps` plus 236 M of the shared expert — so **the MoE block stages
in ~52 s instead of ~25**, and a whole-model run is ~1m32s to first chunk
rather than ~40 s. Residency drops 77.41 -> 76.00 GB in that block (78.53 GB
whole-model with D19's dense bank). Budget the extra minute in every timeout;
`LLM_MOE_BANK=off` is the control.

`go run ./cmd/serve -llm` (added 2026-09-17, research/llm-vertical.md L9a) is the same residency
held open: **33.5 s to stage at `-llm-ctx 4096`**, ~84 GB, and it then serves
until interrupted. A request is a prefill plus ~44 ms a token (22.7 tok/s
through the server on the L8 banks), so a 48-token answer is under a second.
Start it in the background, poll the log for `listening on`, and **kill it
with `pkill -f '[e]xe/serve'` when finished** — the bracket matters, because
`pkill -f 'exe/serve'` matches the shell running it and kills the session
instead (the same trap as [[watch-loops-must-not-match-themselves]]). It holds
the machine for as long as it runs. `-llm-layers 4` is the 7 GB, 3.5 s prefix
and is the right thing for anything about HTTP rather than about the text.

**The access log prints no bodies by default** (`-log-bodies` turns them back
on): a chat server's bodies are conversations. The per-request `llm:` line is
separate and always printed — prompt tokens, how many were reused from the
last turn, and the two rates.

**The model path must name a shard, not the directory.**
`models/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF/` now holds three checkpoints — the model, the
imatrix and the MTP head — so `gguf.OpenSet` refuses it as ambiguous and
`cmd/llm`'s own `-model` default no longer resolves. Pass
`models/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-UD-Q4_K_XL-00001-of-00004.gguf`,
which is what `cmd/serve` defaults to.

**`-layers 24` is the end-to-end instrument when 48 will not fit.** With the
`ai` user service resident (~7 GB) this machine has ~80 GB MemAvailable
against a 48-layer `-graph`'s ~80 GB, which is too tight to schedule. A
24-layer `-graph` is **~40 GB, ~2 min to first number**, and it is a *real*
whole-graph measurement — all five blocks, the head, the host loop, the
per-block ms columns in the CSV — not a block bench. Its one distortion is
that the M-independent fixed costs (head 2.4 ms, `ple`, `move`, host) are 24%
of a step there against 13% at 48 layers, so any *ratio* read off it is
optimistic and the 48-layer number is owed (P5, 2026-09-19).

**How to apply:** run them in the foreground with a long timeout and nothing
else on the GPU, the way [[strix-halo-bench-runs]] asks. `-resident`'s closing
measurement (layer 3's MoE block) is comparable to `-moe -tokens 512 -iters 10`
only at the same iteration count.
---
name: never-edit-source-during-a-sweep
description: "`go run` rebuilds on every invocation, so editing repo source while a multi-arm benchmark script is running kills every arm after the one already in flight."
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

**2026-09-21.** A four-arm 48-layer depth sweep lost three of its four arms.
The script called `go run ./cmd/llm` once per arm; arm 1 had already built and
ran fine; while it ran I edited `shaders/shaders.go` to add a new `//go:embed`
for a `.spv` that did not exist yet, and arms 2-4 each died instantly with

    shaders/shaders.go:2646:12: pattern llm_attn_expand.spv: no matching files found

~25 minutes of measurement, and the failure was silent in the sweep's own log
until the end.

[[strix-halo-bench-runs]] already says "edit *text* while it runs, nothing
else" — that rule is about CPU contention perturbing the numbers. This is a
second, harder reason: **a multi-arm script that invokes `go run` rebuilds the
tree at the start of every arm**, so the source it compiles is whatever the
tree holds *then*, not what it held at launch. Even an edit that compiles
would silently measure a different binary in later arms, which is worse than
a crash.

**How to apply:** make the benchmark script `go build -o <scratchpad>/bench
./cmd/llm` **once at the top** and run that binary for every arm. Then the
tree is free to edit while it runs, and every arm is provably the same build.
Select arms with environment variables read at dispatch time (this is what
`LLM_ATTN_SPLITS` and `LLM_ATTN_CELL_SPLITS` are for), never by rebuilding.
---
name: auto-committer-owns-main
description: "An external process auto-commits the strix-halo-vulkan working tree to main every ~30-45 min with the message \"ai\", and other sessions edit the same tree concurrently, so `go build ./...` can fail on someone else's half-written file."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 8382387e-ec90-4d7d-8642-1d65b8bbd10a
  modified: 2026-09-17T23:25:30.192Z
---

In `~/repos/strix-halo-vulkan` something outside the session commits the whole
working tree to `main` on a timer — the message is always `ai`, and the commits
land roughly every 30-45 minutes (observed 18:53, 19:37, 21:02, 21:36 on
2026-09-14). So a `git add -A && git commit` at the end of a session will often
print **"nothing to commit, working tree clean"** even though the work is
unsaved-looking: check `git show --stat HEAD` before concluding anything was
lost. There is an `origin` (github.com:theninj4/strix-halo-vulkan) but `main`
has **no upstream**, so nothing is pushed.

**Other sessions edit this tree at the same time.** On 2026-09-18 a second
session was mid-refactor in `zimage/pipeline` and mid-write in `api/images.go`
while this one built `embed/`: `go build ./...` failed twice on *their*
undefined symbols (`p.latentH`, `formatSize`), minutes apart, and both cleared
on their own. Check `git status --short` and file mtimes before believing a
build break is yours, and build the packages you touched
(`go build ./embed/ ./api/ …`) rather than `./...` while it lasts.

**Why:** the commit log is therefore not the project's narrative — `TODO.md`
is, and every session appends a handoff to it. That is why the repo's own docs
say to read `TODO.md`/the current vertical file first.

**How to apply:** don't branch before committing here (the whole history is
direct-to-main), don't amend the `ai` commits to "improve" them, and put the
session's story in `TODO.md` rather than in a commit message. Edit files with
targeted replacements rather than whole-file rewrites when another session may
be in the same file, and never "fix" a symbol that belongs to their in-flight
work. See [[strix-halo-bench-runs]] and [[phase-2-pivot-to-pipeline]] for what
the docs expect a session to record.

## Where a decode step goes now

Depth zero, 2048 arena, 28.5 ms a token on the device, 1431 dispatches: the
four weight-streaming kernels (`moe.up` 5.25 ms, `dn.qkv` 4.07, `moe.down`
2.51, the head 2.38) run at roughly 170-200 GB/s, near this device's copy
rate. 898 of the 1431 dispatches are under 12 µs and add up to 3.3 ms; the
196 moves are 0.54 ms of it. What is left of decode is fusion at a percent or
two a step, and L6c's single arena (which would delete the moves) is the
largest of those.

content.content:
## Where 128k stands

48 layers, shipped banks, `wiki.test.raw`, one sequence walked forward,
`-pp 2048 -tg 8 -ctx 139000`, against P13's table at the same shape:

| depth | P13 pp | P14 pp | | P13 tg | P14 tg |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 0 | 1129.3 | 1154.2 | 1.02x | 29.29 | 29.31 |
| 32 000 | 825.8 | **915.6** | 1.11x | 25.84 | 25.80 |
| 64 000 | 719.6 | **892.1** | 1.24x | 24.68 | 24.46 |
| 96 000 | 607.9 | **832.3** | 1.37x | 23.24 | 22.80 |
| **128 000** | **563.6** | **826.0** | **1.47x** | 22.94 | 22.18 |

The falloff from depth zero is **0.72x** where P13 left it at 0.50x and P0 could
not reach the depth at all. **Decode is the control and does not move**: the
gather is prefill's kernel, P14-1's select is bit-identical, and P14-3's score is
a rounding away.

And against the **ubatch**, at 128 000 cells alone (two runs each; `-ctx 139000`
has room for any of these at one depth, and for none but 2048 across five):

| ubatch | pp tok/s at 128 000 | decode |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 2048 | 826.0 | 22.18 |
| 4096 (the shipped `-llm-batch`) | **886.1** | 20.74 |
| 8192 | **946.1** | 18.48 |

That is P12's trade at depth and it is the same trade: a wider ubatch buys the
flat floor and costs decode, so 8192 is a batch summariser's setting and 4096
stays the interactive default.

Where a prefill token goes at 128 000 cells and ubatch 2048, against P13's
budget (ms a token):

	                    P13      P14
	floor              0.803    0.818     everything flat in depth
	attn.attn          0.566    0.303     the gather
	attn.select        0.233    0.021     the block select
	attn.score         0.078    0.034     the matrix cores
	attn.expand        0.051    —         deleted
	attn.gather + mask   —      0.016     what the gather costs
	                 = 1.731  = 1.192

## What is left

- **The union is 3.4x one row's selection** and that is the gathered kernel's
  floor, because the fragment is sixteen rows and the rows are consecutive
  tokens. 2 051 cells a row against 7 049 a tile at 128 000 cells: a per-row
  attention would do 3.4x less work and cannot use a matrix core. Nothing in
  this vertical closes that gap; it is the shape of the hardware against the
  shape of QSA.
- **The floor is now most of a prefill token at depth.** At 128 000 cells and
  ubatch 2048 the attention block is under a third of it and `moe.up` alone is a
  quarter; P11 and P12 established that the MoE prefill GEMM is bound by its
  per-tile slab unpack and that gutting the whole Q4_K scale path is only 1.21x.
- **`maxStorageBufferRange` caps the cache at about 148k cells** and now says so.
  256k needs L6a's array-of-buffers, one a layer — and the guard is what makes
  that a decision rather than a silent wrong answer.
- **`attn.gathmask` is 0.015 ms a token at 128 000 cells**, 5% of the gathered
  attention, and it is the one term here that is a scattered read by nature: the
  per-row mask over the gathered positions. It is already done once for all
  twenty-four heads and already caches the mask word across a run.

## Reproducing

	go build -o /tmp/pp ./cmd/llm        # once, never `go run` per arm
	export LLM_BANK_CACHE=models/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF/bank-cache
	export LLM_DENSE_BANK=deltanet=q4_k/32,hyper_conn=q5_k/32,lm_head=q5_k/32,full_attn=q5_k/32,qsa_indexer=q5_k/32
	export LLM_MOE_BANK=gate_shexp=q4_k,up_shexp=q4_k,down_shexp=q5_1,down_exps=iq4_nl
	M=models/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-UD-Q4_K_XL-00001-of-00004.gguf

	# 128k alone, which is what a wide ubatch has room for at this -ctx.
	# **Do not sweep five depths at ubatch 4096**: the bench raises -ctx to
	# 148520 cells and P14-4 is the error that now stops it.
	/tmp/pp -model $M -depth -depths 128000 -pp 2048 -tg 8 -ctx 139000

	# the fast loop, 40 seconds an arm, and it reproduces the attn.attn ratios
	/tmp/pp -model $M -depth -depths 0,64000,128000 -pp 2048 -tg 4 -ctx 136000 -layers 4

	# the control arms
	LLM_ATTN_GATHER=0            # P13's block kernel
	LLM_ATTN_GATHER_KERNEL=qt1_kt4
	LLM_ATTN_EXPAND_CELLS=1      # P13's cell select, and what Cells() needs
	LLM_ATTN_SCORE=scalar        # P14-3's control

And the whole-model check, which is the cheapest bit-exactness test in the
repo and is worth spelling out here because three of P14's four changes claim
to be bit-exact. `TestGraphLogits` runs 7 tokens through all 48 layers against
llama.cpp's own dump, and it fails on `main` for a reason that predates this

content.text: 24 query heads over 2 KV heads, so 12 query heads share every selection. Reading the gathered attention kernel to see how big a heads-on-rows variant is:

content.content:
1	#version 450
2	
3	#extension GL_KHR_cooperative_matrix : require
4	#extension GL_KHR_memory_scope_semantics : require
5	#extension GL_KHR_shader_subgroup_basic : require
6	#extension GL_KHR_shader_subgroup_clustered : require
7	#extension GL_EXT_shader_16bit_storage : require
8	#extension GL_EXT_shader_explicit_arithmetic_types_float16 : require
9	#extension GL_EXT_control_flow_attributes : require
10	
11	// Causal grouped-query flash attention on the matrix cores, with the output
12	// gate fused into its epilogue: the fourth of the full-attention layer's five
13	// dispatches (LLM.md L2f).
14	//
15	// The flash structure is dit_attention_wmma.comp's and this file does not
16	// re-litigate it — two cooperative-matrix GEMMs with an online softmax between
17	// them, Q held in registers across the whole key loop, the row max taken from
18	// a 16x16 fp32 staging tile because a cooperative matrix's element order is
19	// not defined, the rescale applied as a row-constant matrix, and the softmax
20	// denominator accumulated by appending a column of ones to V. It is a separate
21	// shader rather than another arm of that one because it lives in this
22	// vertical's binding contract (llm_common.glsl, which has a KV cache, an
23	// indexer and a gate where the DiT's has none of them), and because of the two
24	// things below.
25	//
26	// **The head dim is 256, not 128.** HDT doubles to 16, which doubles the query
27	// fragments held in registers and the output accumulators with them: at QT=1
28	// that is 16 A-fragments and 16 accumulators live across the key loop, and it
29	// is why the ladder here starts at QT=1 rather than at the DiT's QT=2. The
30	// arithmetic intensity argument is unchanged and was inert there anyway — what
31	// decides this ladder is the register file.
32	//
33	// **The gate is fused into the store.** `attn_q` is [2560, 12288]: each head's
34	// 256 query dims are immediately followed by 256 *gate* dims, and the gate is
35	// a sigmoid applied to the attention **output**, not to the query. llama.cpp
36	// spends a SIGMOID, a MUL and a CONT on it; here the epilogue already has the
37	// output tile in LDS for the 1/rowSum divide, so the gate costs one extra read
38	// of the fused projection's own fp32 row and the context leaves as fp16
39	// straight into the output projection's A layout. Three of llama.cpp's lines
40	// and a [T, 6144] round trip through DRAM, deleted.
41	//
42	// **The selection is a second mask, and a skip** (P7). `llm_attn_select.comp`
43	// writes one bit per cache cell per token, and this kernel reads it exactly
44	// where it reads the causal one: out of the block row max, so an unselected
45	// cell cannot set the scale, and out of P, which is what removes it from both
46	// O and the row sum. That much is what the reference does — `build_attn_qsa`
47	// turns `top_k` back into an f16 mask and runs **dense** flash attention over
48	// every cell — and on its own it is semantics and not a saving.
49	//
50	// So the mask is also read *before* the key block is, and a block with no
51	// selected cell in any row is skipped whole. The two are the same answer: an
52	// unselected cell contributes nothing to O and nothing to the row sum, so a
53	// block of them contributes nothing, and the skip is bit-identical rather
54	// than an approximation. What it changes is the **cost**, which is the reason
55	// QSA exists: a decode step names 2051 cells however deep the cache is, they
56	// fall in ~513 blocks of `ratio`, and at 64k of context four key blocks in
57	// five hold none of them. At prefill it is close to inert — at ~50% density a
58	// 32-cell block is eight indexer blocks and the chance all eight miss is
59	// ~0.4% (L4b-3) — which is why this is a decode optimisation and only that.
60	//
61	// `selOff == NO_W` is the dense path, and it is the honest one below 2051
62	// cells: at any prompt shorter than `top_k + ratio - 1` the selection names
63	// every cell (research/l2e-attention.md), so running it would be the identity
64	// and the branch is not an approximation.
65	//
66	// **The key range is split across workgroups at decode** (P8, `-DSPLITK`).
67	//
68	// The grid is (query blocks, heads), so a decode step — one token — dispatches
69	// one workgroup a head: 24 of them, each a *single wave*, and each walking
70	// every key block of the cache in turn. They all fit on the device at once,
71	// so the dispatch's wall clock is **one wave's serial walk** and nothing
72	// else: cutting the grid from 24 workgroups to 2 was measured at 1.00x, which
73	// is what says the cost is neither the traffic nor the occupancy across heads
74	// but the length of that walk. Adding heads cannot shorten it; only cutting
75	// the walk can.
76	//
77	// So this build slices the key axis `pc.injOff` ways (ATTN_SPLITS) and gives
78	// each slice its own workgroup — the grid's x becomes (query block, slice) —
79	// and each writes its slice's **unnormalised** context beside the two numbers
80	// an online softmax needs to be resumed: the slice's row max and its row sum.
81	// `llm_attn_combine.comp` puts them back together. That is flash-decoding's
82	// split, and it is exact in the same sense the block loop already is: the
83	// same partial-softmax identity that lets the loop rescale by exp2(mo - mn)
84	// when it meets a bigger max is what lets the combine rescale by
85	// exp2(m_s - m*) when it meets the largest of the slices'.
86	//
87	// It is **not bit-identical** to the unsplit kernel and cannot be: the
88	// rescales happen in a different order and fp32 addition is not associative.
89	// What it is is the same arithmetic, gated on agreement with the reference
90	// rather than with the other kernel — see TestAttnGPUSplitMatchesDense.
91	//
92	// **The query is a batch, the key and the value are a cache** (L7a). Row i of
93	// query block q0 is cell `SEQ_PAST + q0 + i` and the keys run over every cell
94	// the cache holds, `SEQ_PAST + tokens` of them, so the two operands no longer
95	// share a plane geometry: the query's is `plane` padded token rows, the key's
96	// and the value's are nKV cells. Every causal comparison is between a cell and
97	// a *position*, and on a fresh sequence SEQ_PAST is zero and all of it is
98	// what L2f measured.
99	
100	#include "llm_common.glsl"
101	
102	#ifndef QT
103	#define QT 1        // query tiles per wave
104	#endif
105	#ifndef KTIL
106	#define KTIL 4      // key tiles per block
107	#endif
108	#ifndef WAVE
109	#define WAVE 64
110	#endif
111	#ifndef HEAD_DIM
112	#define HEAD_DIM 256
113	#endif
114	
115	#define TILE 16
116	#define HDT (HEAD_DIM / TILE)
117	#define BM (QT * TILE)
118	#define BN (KTIL * TILE)
119	
120	// The row max's lane split (P12). The scan below is one row per lane at
121	// BM=16 on a 64-wide wave, which is sixteen lanes of sixty-four; RCL lanes
122	// share a row instead, each taking RCPL of the block's BN columns, and a
123	// clustered subgroup max folds them. Every shipped rung has BM <= 32 < WAVE,
124	// so RCL is 4 or 2; the `RCL <= 1` arm below is what a QT=4 build would take
125	// and keeps the file honest rather than being reachable today.
126	#define RCL (WAVE / BM)
127	#define RCPL (BN / RCL)
128	
129	// Mask words a row a key block. **It is not BN/32**, because BN may be
130	// narrower than a word: a 16-cell key block (KTIL=1) is half of one, so the
131	// staged slice is still one word a row and the block's cells start at bit
132	// `base & 31` inside it. Every wider rung has `base` a multiple of 32 and
133	// `SELBIT` is zero, which is exactly the addressing this had before.
134	#define BW ((BN + 31) / 32)
135	#define SELBIT(base) ((BN < 32) ? ((base) & 31u) : 0u)
136	
137	// **Query heads a workgroup** (P14-2, fourth pass), and it is the gathered
138	// kernel's only structural knob.
139	//
140	// The probe that motivates it: doubling the QK matrix work costs **2.7%**, so
141	// the gathered kernel is not arithmetic-bound at all — it is bound by the gather
142	// itself. A key chunk moves 32 KB of global reads, 32 KB of LDS writes and 32 KB
143	// of LDS reads per wave, and the first two are **the same bytes for every query
144	// head that shares a kv head**: the grid is (query tile, head), the selection is
145	// per token, and this model has twelve query heads to a kv head. Putting HPW
146	// heads in one workgroup stages once for all of them.
147	//
148	// Each wave still owns one head and its own registers, so nothing about the
149	// fragments or the online softmax changes; what becomes per wave is the LDS the
150	// softmax uses, and what becomes shared is the staged key, the cell list and the
151	// mask. `HPW = 1` is the arrangement this kernel had, and every offset below
152	// folds to zero there — which is what keeps the block and split builds, which
153	// have no business with this, byte for byte what they were.
154	#ifndef HPW
155	#define HPW 1
156	#endif
157	#if HPW > 1 && !defined(GATHER)
158	#error "HPW is the gathered kernel's knob; the block and split builds are one wave"
159	#endif
160	
161	layout(local_size_x = WAVE * HPW) in;
162	
163	#define ACC  coopmat<float, gl_ScopeSubgroup, TILE, TILE, gl_MatrixUseAccumulator>
164	#define ACCH coopmat<float16_t, gl_ScopeSubgroup, TILE, TILE, gl_MatrixUseAccumulator>
165	#define FRAG_A coopmat<float16_t, gl_ScopeSubgroup, TILE, TILE, gl_MatrixUseA>
166	#define FRAG_B coopmat<float16_t, gl_ScopeSubgroup, TILE, TILE, gl_MatrixUseB>
167	
168	// The score staging tile, and it holds the **whole key block** rather than one
169	// key tile of it (P12): all QT*KTIL of the block's score fragments at once, so
170	// the row max below is one pass over BM x BN with one barrier in front of it
171	// instead of KTIL passes with two each. Everything after the row max uses only
172	// the first QT tiles of it, exactly as it did when that was all there was.
173	// Per **wave**, not per workgroup: at HPW > 1 each wave is a different head with
174	// its own softmax, so these are sharded and `sBase`/`pBase`/`bBase`/`rBase` in
175	// main() are the wave's slice. At HPW = 1 every base is zero and folds away.
176	#define SSTAGE (QT * KTIL * TILE * TILE)
177	#define SPBUF  (BM * BN)
178	#define SBCORR (QT * TILE * TILE)
179	shared float stage[HPW * SSTAGE];
180	shared float16_t pbuf[HPW * SPBUF];
181	shared float bcorr[HPW * SBCORR];
182	shared float rowMax[HPW * BM];
183	shared float blkMax[HPW * BM];
184	shared float rowSum[HPW * BM];
185	// This key block's slice of the QSA bitmask, one word per (row, 32 cells).
186	// It is staged once a block rather than bit-tested out of the arena per
187	// element: the mask loop below touches BM*BN elements and the row max another
188	// BM*TILE, which is 512 global reads a block where the block's whole mask is
189	// BM*BN/32 words. Reading it per element cost the kernel 1.90x.
190	shared uint selw[BM * BW];
191	// Whether any row of this key block has any cell selected at all.
192	shared uint blkAny;
193	
194	#ifdef GATHER
195	// The staging barrier, and it is **a workgroup barrier and not a subgroup one**
196	// — which is a measurement and then a correctness requirement.
197	//
198	// The measurement: at HPW = 1 this kernel's workgroup is exactly one subgroup, so
199	// `subgroupMemoryBarrierShared()` gives the double-buffered loop the LDS ordering
200	// it needs without the `s_barrier` that `barrier()` also emits. A key chunk
201	// carries 32 of these against 66 matrix ops, so it looked worth having — and it
202	// is **1.00x**, as is staging two head-dim groups per barrier (GRP=2) and as is
203	// P13-3's compaction and P11-4's hoist before it. *Latency that matters at decode
204	// does not matter at prefill, because prefill has occupancy.* Fourth time.
205	//
206	// The requirement: at HPW > 1 the staging loop spans every wave of the
207	// workgroup, and a subgroup barrier orders none of it. So it is `barrier()`,
208	// which is what the measurement says it may as well be.
209	#define GSTAGE_BARRIER() barrier()
210	
211	// P14-2's gathered key chunk, one head-dim group at a time.
212	//
213	// **It is 512 halves and that is the whole design.** A gathered cell's sixteen
214	// dims for group `kt` are 32 contiguous bytes in the plane and the plane is not
215	// contiguous in the *cells*, so a fragment over scattered cells cannot be a
216	// `coopMatLoad` from the arena — it has to be staged. Staging the chunk's whole
217	// 256 dims at once would be 16 KB at BN=32 and 32 KB at BN=64, and a
218	// single-wave workgroup that takes 32 KB of LDS is two workgroups resident per
219	// 64 KB where this kernel today gets twenty — which is the one thing a prefill
220	// cannot give up (P13-3: *latency and redundant reads that matter at decode do
221	// not matter at prefill, because prefill has occupancy*). Staged a group at a
222	// time it is `KTIL * 256` halves, 1 KB at the shipped rung, and the QK loop was
223	// already iterating the groups.
224	//
225	// Both planes read it: the key as a ColumnMajor B operand — element (dim, cell)
226	// at `cell*TILE + dim` — and the value as a RowMajor one, element (cell, dim)
227	// at the same address, because P14-2 made the value plane cell-major too. One
228	// layout, one staging loop.
229	// **Two of them** (P14-2's second pass): group `g` is staged while the matrix
230	// cores are still working on group `g-1`, so the QK and PV loops carry one
231	// barrier each per group instead of two — one to say the buffer being read is
232	// complete, where a single buffer also needed one to say it had been read before
233	// it was overwritten. A key chunk is 32 groups of staging and two barriers a
234	// group was comparable with the mma it was feeding.
235	// **GRP head-dim groups a staging call** (P14-2, third pass). Double buffering
236	// took the barriers from two a group to one; staging GRP groups at a time takes
237	// them to one per GRP. It costs LDS — `2 * GRP * KTIL * 256` halves, 2 KB at
238	// GRP=1 and 4 KB at GRP=2 on the shipped rung — and LDS is occupancy, so it is a
239	// build knob and the ladder decides.
240	#ifndef GRP
241	#define GRP 1
242	#endif
243	#if (HDT % GRP) != 0
244	#error "GRP must divide the head-dim groups"
245	#endif
246	#define GSTAGE (KTIL * TILE * TILE)
247	shared float16_t kvs[2][GRP * GSTAGE];
248	// The mask pass rounds its write up to GATH_BW words a row, so a rung that
249	// staged more than that per chunk would read words nothing wrote.
250	#if BW > 2
251	#error "a gathered rung stages more mask words a chunk than llm_attn_gather.comp writes (GATH_BW)"
252	#endif
253	// This chunk's cell indices, staged once for both planes and all HDT groups.
254	shared uint glist[BN];
255	#endif
256	
257	#if !defined(SPLITK) && !defined(GATHER)
258	// P13's live-block list, a chunk at a time. `pc.resOff` names an ascending
259	// list of the key blocks this query tile has anything selected in, with the
260	// count in front of it, and this kernel then iterates the list instead of the
261	// axis — which is what makes a prefill flat in depth, because the live count
262	// is (515, 518, 696) at (32k, 64k, 128k) where the axis is (1000, 2000,
263	// 4000).
264	//
265	// It is staged rather than read per iteration for the reason the mask was
266	// (L4b-3): the loop below is one wave, so a scalar load at the top of every
267	// block is a dependent global read on the critical path. A chunk of LCHUNK
268	// is one coalesced read per LCHUNK blocks.
269	//
270	// **Bit-identical, and not merely close.** The list holds exactly the blocks
271	// the `blkAny` skip would not have skipped, in the order the loop would have
272	// met them, so the same partial softmaxes are folded in the same order. What
273	// is deleted is the visit to the blocks that contributed nothing — which P7
274	// already established contribute nothing.
275	#define LCHUNK 256
276	shared uint blist[LCHUNK];
277	#endif
278	
279	#ifdef GATHER
280	// Where this build reads the gathered list from, and it is not the same field
281	// in both builds because the split needs `resOff` for something else.
282	//
283	// The unsplit gathered kernel writes its answer straight out and reads the list
284	// through `resOff`, as P14-2 left it. The split one writes *partials*, and the
285	// partial arena is what `resOff` means to every SPLITK build and to
286	// `llm_attn_combine.comp` behind them — so the list moves to `cellOff`, which
287	// is free here: it is the indexer's expanded per-cell score, which P14-1
288	// deleted and which no attention build has ever read. The push block is full at
289	// 64 uints (TestAttnGPUPushBlockFits), so a spare field is the whole budget
290	// there is.
291	#ifdef SPLITK
292	#define GATH_BASE pc.cellOff
293	#else

297	// stagePlane loads one head-dim group of this chunk's gathered cells into LDS:
298	// cell `c` of the chunk takes its sixteen halves from
299	// `plane + (cell/16 * HDT + grp) * 256 + (cell%16) * 16`, and lands at
300	// `c * TILE` — the layout both `coopMatLoad`s above want.
301	//
302	// Eight halves a lane, unrolled over constant offsets so the load is one
303	// 16-byte transfer and the store one LDS write. A selected run is `ratio`
304	// consecutive cells, so consecutive `c` are consecutive 32-byte pieces of the
305	// same tile and a run of four is one 128-byte line — which is the reason the
306	// value plane moved to cell-major.
307	//
308	// Positions past the chunk's own count stage as **zero**: their mask bits are
309	// zero so nothing reads the score they produce, and a zero is cheaper to be
310	// sure about than a bounds test inside the fragment.
311	void stagePlane(uint tid, uint buf, uint planeBase, uint grp0, uint cnt) {
312	    for (uint i = tid; i < GRP * BN * 2u; i += WAVE * HPW) {
313	        uint g = i / (BN * 2u), rem = i % (BN * 2u);
314	        uint c = rem >> 1u, half8 = (rem & 1u) * 8u;
315	        uint dst = g * GSTAGE + c * TILE + half8;
316	        if (c >= cnt) {
317	            [[unroll]] for (uint d = 0u; d < 8u; ++d) {
318	                kvs[buf][dst + d] = float16_t(0.0);
319	            }
320	            continue;
321	        }
322	        uint cell = glist[c];
323	        uint src = planeBase + ((cell / TILE) * HDT + grp0 + g) * (TILE * TILE)
324	            + (cell % TILE) * TILE + half8;
325	        [[unroll]] for (uint d = 0u; d < 8u; ++d) {
326	            kvs[buf][dst + d] = hact[src + d];
327	        }
328	    }
329	}
330	#endif

332	// stageSel loads this key block's slice of the QSA bitmask into LDS: one word
333	// per (row, 32 cells), read by both the row max and the mask loop below, and
334	// returns the OR of the words this lane staged — which is how the skip below
335	// learns whether the block has anything in it at all.
336	//
337	// `base` is a multiple of BN; where BN is a multiple of 32 a word of the
338	// staged slice is a word of the arena, and where it is not (KTIL=1, a 16-cell
339	// block) the row's word is the one containing `base` and the block is the
340	// half of it at `SELBIT`. Either way nothing is shifted: the bit index does
341	// the work, so a rung change costs no extra instruction on the rungs that
342	// were already word-aligned. A pad row has no
343	// selection — llm_attn_select.comp does not run past the prompt — so it stages
344	// as **zero**: nothing of it is visible, its softmax denominator is zero, and
345	// the epilogue turns that into a zero row rather than a NaN. (It used to stage
346	// all-ones and take the dense path for exactly that denominator; the skip
347	// below would then have been defeated by fifteen pad rows on every decode
348	// step, which is the one shape where the skip is worth anything.)
349	uint stageSel(uint lane, uint q0, uint base) {
350	    uint words = (pc.nKV + 31u) / 32u;
351	    // The bits of the staged word this key block actually covers: all of them
352	    // on a word-aligned rung, the 16 at SELBIT on a 16-cell one. The skip
353	    // below must not be defeated by a neighbouring block's bits.
354	    uint keep = (BN < 32) ? (((1u << BN) - 1u) << SELBIT(base)) : 0xFFFFFFFFu;
355	    uint acc = 0u;
356	    for (uint i = lane; i < BM * BW; i += WAVE) {
357	        uint row = i / BW, wd = i % BW;
358	        uint token = q0 + row;
359	        uint w = (token >= pc.tokens) ? 0u
360	                                      : actu[pc.selOff + token * words + ((base + wd * 32u) >> 5u)];
361	        selw[i] = w;
362	        acc |= w & keep;
363	    }
364	    return acc;
365	}

367	// selected reads one bit out of the staged slice. `bit0` is the block's first
368	// bit inside its row's first staged word, which is zero on every rung whose
369	// key block is a whole number of words.
370	bool selected(uint row, uint col, uint bit0) {
371	    uint b = bit0 + col;
372	    return (selw[row * BW + (b >> 5u)] & (1u << (b & 31u))) != 0u;
373	}

759	            coopMatLoad(ccorr, bcorr, bBase + qq * (TILE * TILE), TILE, gl_CooperativeMatrixLayoutRowMajor);

761	                ACC p = s[qq][kk] - mrow;
762	                [[unroll]] for (uint e = 0u; e < p.length(); ++e) {
763	                    p[e] = exp2(p[e]);

766	                    gl_CooperativeMatrixLayoutRowMajor);

772	        }
773	        barrier();
774	
775	        // Mask the pad keys and the future ones out of P, which is what
776	        // removes them from both O and the row sums. Without a selection only
777	        // the diagonal block needs it — every earlier block is entirely in the
778	        // past of every row — but the selection drops cells anywhere, so with
779	        // it on every block passes through here.
780	#ifdef GATHER
781	        // **One predicate, and it is the mask** (P14-2). The causal test is
782	        // already in it — the gather ANDed each row's own extent into the bits
783	        // it wrote — and the positions past this chunk's count carry a zero bit
784	        // for every row, so the `col >= cnt` test goes with it.

786	            if (!selected(i / BN, i & (BN - 1u), selBit)) {

788	            }
789	        }
790	        barrier();
791	#else
792	        if (sparse || cnt < BN || base + BN > past + q0) {
793	            for (uint i = lane; i < BM * BN; i += WAVE) {
794	                uint col = i & (BN - 1u);
795	                uint row = i / BN;
796	                if (col >= cnt || base + col > past + q0 + row ||
797	                    (sparse && !selected(row, col, selBit))) {
798	                    pbuf[pBase + i] = float16_t(0.0);

800	            }
801	            barrier();
802	        }
803	#endif

805	        FRAG_A fragP[QT][KTIL];
806	        [[unroll]] for (uint qq = 0u; qq < QT; ++qq) {
807	            [[unroll]] for (uint kk = 0u; kk < KTIL; ++kk) {
808	                coopMatLoad(fragP[qq][kk], pbuf, pBase + (qq * TILE) * BN + kk * TILE, BN,
809	                    gl_CooperativeMatrixLayoutRowMajor);
810	            }
811	        }
812	#ifdef GATHER
813	        stagePlane(tid, 0u, vBase, 0u, cnt);
814	#endif
815	        [[unroll]] for (uint j = 0u; j < HDT; ++j) {
816	            FRAG_B fragV[KTIL];
817	#ifdef GATHER
818	            if (j % GRP == 0u) {
819	                GSTAGE_BARRIER();
820	                if (j + GRP < HDT) {
821	                    stagePlane(tid, ((j / GRP) + 1u) & 1u, vBase, j + GRP, cnt);
822	                }
823	            }
824	            [[unroll]] for (uint kk = 0u; kk < KTIL; ++kk) {
825	                coopMatLoad(fragV[kk], kvs[(j / GRP) & 1u],
826	                    (j % GRP) * GSTAGE + kk * (TILE * TILE),
827	                    TILE, gl_CooperativeMatrixLayoutRowMajor);
828	            }
829	#else
830	            [[unroll]] for (uint kk = 0u; kk < KTIL; ++kk) {
831	                // **RowMajor, because the value plane is cell-major** (P14-2):
832	                // element (k=cell, n=dim) at `k*TILE + n`. It was ColumnMajor
833	                // over a transposed tile and is the same matrix either way —
834	                // see the note in llm_attn_pack.comp for why the layout moved.
835	                coopMatLoad(fragV[kk], hact, vBase + ((base / TILE + kk) * HDT + j) * (TILE * TILE),
836	                    TILE, gl_CooperativeMatrixLayoutRowMajor);
837	            }
838	#endif
839	            [[unroll]] for (uint qq = 0u; qq < QT; ++qq) {
840	                [[unroll]] for (uint kk = 0u; kk < KTIL; ++kk) {
841	                    o[qq][j] = coopMatMulAdd(fragP[qq][kk], fragV[kk], o[qq][j]);
842	                }
843	            }
844	        }

846	            [[unroll]] for (uint kk = 0u; kk < KTIL; ++kk) {
847	                lsum[qq] = coopMatMulAdd(fragP[qq][kk], ones, lsum[qq]);

854	#ifdef SPLITK
855	    // ---- The split epilogue: this slice's partial, and how to resume it.
856	    //
857	    // Nothing is normalised and nothing is gated here — `o` is still relative
858	    // to this slice's own row max and `lsum` is still this slice's own
859	    // denominator, because neither is the row's until every slice has been
860	    // seen. The combine does the divide and the gate, once, off the assembled
861	    // row. A slice that got no block writes -inf and zero, which is the
862	    // identity there.

864	        coopMatStore(lsum[qq], stage, sBase + qq * (TILE * TILE), TILE,
865	            gl_CooperativeMatrixLayoutRowMajor);
866	    }
867	    barrier();
868	    for (uint i = lane; i < BM; i += WAVE) {
869	        uint qi = i / TILE, r = i % TILE;
870	        rowSum[rBase + i] = stage[sBase + qi * (TILE * TILE) + r * TILE];
871	    }
872	    barrier();
873	
874	    // The partial arena, ATTN_SPLIT (llm_common.glsl): the contexts first,
875	    // [heads][splits][tokens][headDim], then the pair per row behind them.
876	    uint slice = (head * splits + sp) * pc.tokens;
877	    uint mlBase = pc.resOff + pc.heads * splits * pc.tokens * pc.headDim;
878	    for (uint i = lane; i < BM; i += WAVE) {
879	        uint token = q0 + i;
880	        if (token < pc.tokens) {
881	            uint at = mlBase + (slice + token) * 2u;
882	            act[at] = rowMax[rBase + i];
883	            act[at + 1u] = rowSum[rBase + i];
884	        }
885	    }
886	    barrier();
887	
888	    [[unroll]] for (uint j = 0u; j < HDT; ++j) {
889	        [[unroll]] for (uint qq = 0u; qq < QT; ++qq) {
890	            coopMatStore(o[qq][j], stage, sBase + qq * (TILE * TILE), TILE,
891	                gl_CooperativeMatrixLayoutRowMajor);
892	        }
893	        barrier();
894	        // Four lanes a row, four floats each, as the gated store below. The
895	        // pad rows are skipped rather than written: unlike the context arena
896	        // this one is read back by a kernel that knows how many rows are
897	        // real, so there is nothing for a pad row to keep clean.
898	        for (uint i = lane; i < BM * 4u; i += WAVE) {
899	            uint row = i / 4u, part = i % 4u;
900	            uint token = q0 + row;
901	            if (token >= pc.tokens) {
902	                continue;
903	            }
904	            uint qi = row / TILE, r = row % TILE;
905	            uint src = qi * (TILE * TILE) + r * TILE + part * 4u;
906	            uint dst = pc.resOff + (slice + token) * pc.headDim + j * TILE + part * 4u;
907	            [[unroll]] for (uint c = 0u; c < 4u; ++c) {
908	                act[dst + c] = stage[sBase + src + c];
909	            }
910	        }
911	        barrier();
912	    }
913	}

915	    // ---- Epilogue: the softmax divide and the output gate, together.
916	    //
917	    // Every column of lsum holds the row sum, so column 0 is read out of a
918	    // staging tile. The output goes through the same tile rather than being
919	    // stored as a matrix, because the gate is indexed by (row, column) and a
920	    // cooperative matrix's element order is not defined — which is the same
921	    // reason the row max needed a staging tile.
922	    [[unroll]] for (uint qq = 0u; qq < QT; ++qq) {
923	        coopMatStore(lsum[qq], stage, sBase + qq * (TILE * TILE), TILE,
924	            gl_CooperativeMatrixLayoutRowMajor);
925	    }
926	    barrier();
927	    for (uint i = lane; i < BM; i += WAVE) {
928	        uint qi = i / TILE, r = i % TILE;
929	        rowSum[rBase + i] = stage[sBase + qi * (TILE * TILE) + r * TILE];
930	    }
931	    barrier();
932	
933	    uint gateCol = pc.qkvOff + head * 2u * pc.headDim + pc.headDim;
934	    [[unroll]] for (uint j = 0u; j < HDT; ++j) {
935	        [[unroll]] for (uint qq = 0u; qq < QT; ++qq) {
936	            coopMatStore(o[qq][j], stage, sBase + qq * (TILE * TILE), TILE,
937	                gl_CooperativeMatrixLayoutRowMajor);
938	        }
939	        barrier();
940	        // Four lanes per row, four contiguous halves each. The rows past the
941	        // prompt are written too rather than branched around: they are the
942	        // output projection's pad rows, whose products nothing reads.
943	        for (uint i = lane; i < BM * 4u; i += WAVE) {
944	            uint row = i / 4u, part = i % 4u;

949	            // never read — it is the output projection's padding — but a NaN
950	            // there would be a NaN in an arena the next pass reuses, so it is
951	            // written as a zero row instead.
952	            float inv = (rowSum[rBase + row] > 0.0) ? 1.0 / rowSum[rBase + row] : 0.0;
953	            uint src = qi * (TILE * TILE) + r * TILE + part * 4u;
954	            uint d0 = j * TILE + part * 4u;
955	            uint dst = pc.ctxOff + token * pc.ldCtx + head * pc.headDim + d0;
956	            [[unroll]] for (uint c = 0u; c < 4u; ++c) {
957	                float g = act[gateCol + token * pc.gemmN + d0 + c];
958	                hact[dst + c] = float16_t(stage[sBase + src + c] * inv / (1.0 + exp(-g)));

960	        }
961	        barrier();

11	// Causal grouped-query flash attention on the matrix cores, with the output
12	// gate fused into its epilogue: the fourth of the full-attention layer's five
13	// dispatches (LLM.md L2f).
14	//
15	// The flash structure is dit_attention_wmma.comp's and this file does not
16	// re-litigate it — two cooperative-matrix GEMMs with an online softmax between
17	// them, Q held in registers across the whole key loop, the row max taken from
18	// a 16x16 fp32 staging tile because a cooperative matrix's element order is
19	// not defined, the rescale applied as a row-constant matrix, and the softmax
20	// denominator accumulated by appending a column of ones to V. It is a separate
21	// shader rather than another arm of that one because it lives in this
22	// vertical's binding contract (llm_common.glsl, which has a KV cache, an
23	// indexer and a gate where the DiT's has none of them), and because of the two
24	// things below.
25	//
26	// **The head dim is 256, not 128.** HDT doubles to 16, which doubles the query
27	// fragments held in registers and the output accumulators with them: at QT=1
28	// that is 16 A-fragments and 16 accumulators live across the key loop, and it
29	// is why the ladder here starts at QT=1 rather than at the DiT's QT=2. The
30	// arithmetic intensity argument is unchanged and was inert there anyway — what
31	// decides this ladder is the register file.
32	//
33	// **The gate is fused into the store.** `attn_q` is [2560, 12288]: each head's
34	// 256 query dims are immediately followed by 256 *gate* dims, and the gate is
35	// a sigmoid applied to the attention **output**, not to the query. llama.cpp
36	// spends a SIGMOID, a MUL and a CONT on it; here the epilogue already has the
37	// output tile in LDS for the 1/rowSum divide, so the gate costs one extra read
38	// of the fused projection's own fp32 row and the context leaves as fp16
39	// straight into the output projection's A layout. Three of llama.cpp's lines
40	// and a [T, 6144] round trip through DRAM, deleted.
41	//
42	// **The selection is a second mask, and a skip** (P7). `llm_attn_select.comp`
43	// writes one bit per cache cell per token, and this kernel reads it exactly
44	// where it reads the causal one: out of the block row max, so an unselected
45	// cell cannot set the scale, and out of P, which is what removes it from both
46	// O and the row sum. That much is what the reference does — `build_attn_qsa`
47	// turns `top_k` back into an f16 mask and runs **dense** flash attention over
48	// every cell — and on its own it is semantics and not a saving.
49	//
50	// So the mask is also read *before* the key block is, and a block with no
51	// selected cell in any row is skipped whole. The two are the same answer: an
52	// unselected cell contributes nothing to O and nothing to the row sum, so a
53	// block of them contributes nothing, and the skip is bit-identical rather
54	// than an approximation. What it changes is the **cost**, which is the reason
55	// QSA exists: a decode step names 2051 cells however deep the cache is, they
56	// fall in ~513 blocks of `ratio`, and at 64k of context four key blocks in
57	// five hold none of them. At prefill it is close to inert — at ~50% density a
58	// 32-cell block is eight indexer blocks and the chance all eight miss is
59	// ~0.4% (L4b-3) — which is why this is a decode optimisation and only that.
60	//
61	// `selOff == NO_W` is the dense path, and it is the honest one below 2051
62	// cells: at any prompt shorter than `top_k + ratio - 1` the selection names
63	// every cell (research/l2e-attention.md), so running it would be the identity
64	// and the branch is not an approximation.
65	//
66	// **The key range is split across workgroups at decode** (P8, `-DSPLITK`).
67	//
68	// The grid is (query blocks, heads), so a decode step — one token — dispatches
69	// one workgroup a head: 24 of them, each a *single wave*, and each walking
70	// every key block of the cache in turn. They all fit on the device at once,
71	// so the dispatch's wall clock is **one wave's serial walk** and nothing
72	// else: cutting the grid from 24 workgroups to 2 was measured at 1.00x, which
73	// is what says the cost is neither the traffic nor the occupancy across heads
74	// but the length of that walk. Adding heads cannot shorten it; only cutting
75	// the walk can.
76	//
77	// So this build slices the key axis `pc.injOff` ways (ATTN_SPLITS) and gives
78	// each slice its own workgroup — the grid's x becomes (query block, slice) —
79	// and each writes its slice's **unnormalised** context beside the two numbers
80	// an online softmax needs to be resumed: the slice's row max and its row sum.
81	// `llm_attn_combine.comp` puts them back together. That is flash-decoding's
82	// split, and it is exact in the same sense the block loop already is: the
83	// same partial-softmax identity that lets the loop rescale by exp2(mo - mn)
84	// when it meets a bigger max is what lets the combine rescale by

86	//

39	// straight into the output projection's A layout. Three of llama.cpp's lines
40	// and a [T, 6144] round trip through DRAM, deleted.
41	//
42	// **The selection is a second mask, and a skip** (P7). `llm_attn_select.comp`
43	// writes one bit per cache cell per token, and this kernel reads it exactly
44	// where it reads the causal one: out of the block row max, so an unselected
45	// cell cannot set the scale, and out of P, which is what removes it from both
46	// O and the row sum. That much is what the reference does — `build_attn_qsa`
47	// turns `top_k` back into an f16 mask and runs **dense** flash attention over
48	// every cell — and on its own it is semantics and not a saving.
49	//
50	// So the mask is also read *before* the key block is, and a block with no
51	// selected cell in any row is skipped whole. The two are the same answer: an
52	// unselected cell contributes nothing to O and nothing to the row sum, so a
53	// block of them contributes nothing, and the skip is bit-identical rather
54	// than an approximation. What it changes is the **cost**, which is the reason
55	// QSA exists: a decode step names 2051 cells however deep the cache is, they
56	// fall in ~513 blocks of `ratio`, and at 64k of context four key blocks in
57	// five hold none of them. At prefill it is close to inert — at ~50% density a
58	// 32-cell block is eight indexer blocks and the chance all eight miss is
59	// ~0.4% (L4b-3) — which is why this is a decode optimisation and only that.
60	//
61	// `selOff == NO_W` is the dense path, and it is the honest one below 2051
62	// cells: at any prompt shorter than `top_k + ratio - 1` the selection names
63	// every cell (research/l2e-attention.md), so running it would be the identity
64	// and the branch is not an approximation.
65	//
66	// **The key range is split across workgroups at decode** (P8, `-DSPLITK`).
67	//
68	// The grid is (query blocks, heads), so a decode step — one token — dispatches
69	// one workgroup a head: 24 of them, each a *single wave*, and each walking
70	// every key block of the cache in turn. They all fit on the device at once,
71	// so the dispatch's wall clock is **one wave's serial walk** and nothing
72	// else: cutting the grid from 24 workgroups to 2 was measured at 1.00x, which
73	// is what says the cost is neither the traffic nor the occupancy across heads
74	// but the length of that walk. Adding heads cannot shorten it; only cutting
75	// the walk can.
76	//
77	// So this build slices the key axis `pc.injOff` ways (ATTN_SPLITS) and gives
78	// each slice its own workgroup — the grid's x becomes (query block, slice) —
79	// and each writes its slice's **unnormalised** context beside the two numbers
80	// an online softmax needs to be resumed: the slice's row max and its row sum.

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

# P17 — heads on the fragment's rows: 128k prefills past 1000 tok/s

**2026-09-22.** One change. A 128 000-cell prefill at ubatch 2048 goes
**833.5 → 1011.4 tok/s (1.21x)**, 64 000 cells **896.4 → 1048.6 (1.17x)**, and
the prefill falloff from depth zero goes from **0.72x to 0.88x**. Decode at depth gains
**~2%** because the mask pass is gone (31.62 → 32.21 tok/s at 128k), and a
decode step's answer is **bit-identical**.

| depth | pp before | pp after | | tg before | tg after |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 0 | 1156.6 | 1156.3 ¹ | 1.00x | 34.39 | 34.34 |
| 4 096 | 1015.4 | **1049.1** | 1.03x | 33.33 | **34.10** |
| 64 000 | 896.4 | **1048.6** | **1.17x** | 32.17 | **32.97** |
| 128 000 | 833.5 | **1011.4** | **1.21x** | 31.62 | **32.21** |

48 layers, shipped banks, `-pp 2048 -tg 16 -ctx 139000`, `wiki.test.raw`,
same binary, arms selected by `LLM_ATTN_GATHER_HROWS`. Two interleaved runs a
arm at 0/64k/128k (agreeing to 0.2%, the table is their mean:
`results/p17_ab48_h{0,1}_r{1,2}.csv`), one at 0/4096 with the default rule
against the control (`results/p17_rule_{def,0}.csv`).
¹ The default rule, which takes the token-row kernel at depth 0. Forcing the
heads build there (`LLM_ATTN_GATHER_HROWS=1`) is 1144.3, −1.1% — see below.

## The idea

P14's gathered attention puts sixteen consecutive **tokens** of one query head
on a cooperative-matrix fragment's M axis, and reads the **union** of their
QSA selections. At 128 000 cells that is 7 049 cells a tile where one token
selects 2 051. P14 called that 3.4x "the shape of the hardware against the
shape of QSA", something nothing in this vertical closes.

But the selection is per **token**, not per head, and this model has 24 query
heads over 2 kv heads. The twelve heads of one token are twelve rows that attend
over **exactly the same cells** of **exactly the same key and value**. Put them
on M instead:

- **The list is one token's selection**, 2 051 cells, not a sixteen-token
  union. The gather's existing `BM=1` build writes it (pass 1 only).
- **There is no per-row mask.** Every row wants every gathered cell, so the
  `attn.gathmask` dispatch is gone. The kernel's only predicate is `col < cnt`
  on a short last chunk.
- **The kv plane is staged once for twelve heads**, not once a head.
  That is the sharing P14's `HPW` knob tried, at 12x instead of 2x.
- **The Q fragment needs no repack.** The plane is head-major, tiled 16 tokens
  by 16 dims, so row `r` of (token t, dim group kt) is sixteen contiguous halves
  one head's plane apart: a RowMajor `coopMatLoad` with a stride of one head.

Rows are heads `h0 .. h0+15` with `h0 = min(g*rep, heads-16)`. The four rows
belonging to the other kv head are computed against the wrong key and never
stored, which is cheaper than any test inside the fragment and keeps every Q
load inside the plane. 12 of 16 rows are useful. Against the 2 051/7 049 the
token rows got at 128k, that is the whole win. The grid is (token, kv head),
or (token·splits + slice, kv head) split.

`attn.attn` at 128k, 48 layers: **51.6 → 15.9 ms a pass, 3.25x** (0.302 →
0.093 ms a token). On the 4-layer probe, whose one attention layer is denser
than the mean, it is 77.2 → 16.8 ms, 4.6x.

## Where it loses, and the rule

From a cold cache the selection names every live cell, so a token tile's union
*is* one row's, and heads-on-rows only wastes a quarter of the fragment. On the
4-layer probe (tok/s, two runs each, `results/p17_cross_h{0,1}.csv`):

	past        0     2048    4096    8192   16384  128000
	tokens  11109   10406   10162    9818    9424    7817
	heads   11076   10504   10590   10529   10500   10271

At 48 layers and ctx 139 000 the depth-0 loss is 1.1% (5.40 → 6.58 ms of
`attn.attn` a pass). So prefill takes heads-on-rows only when
`past >= selWidth` (`LLM_ATTN_GATHER_HROWS_MIN` overrides). Decode always
takes it once it gathers, because there the two builds are the same bits.

## Exactness

**Decode is bit-identical**, and the gate asserts a zero. At one row, the
token fragment's union *is* the token's selection, so both kernels fold the
same cells in the same chunks in the same order. A matrix product's rows are
independent, so which fragment row a head lands in does not change its sums. What
decode gains is the deleted mask dispatch (6.6 µs a layer) and a gather that
no longer ORs sixteen rows.

**Prefill is a reassociation**, like P14-2: the same set, folded in different
chunks. 3.6e-05 relative rms from the token-row kernel against 1.2e-02 of
either from llama.cpp, and against the block kernel 4.31e-06 where the token-row
gather is 4.10e-06. It falls under `PinSchedule` with the gather it rides on,
so nothing new there.

Gates:

	go test ./llm/ -run TestAttnGPUHeadRowsIsTheGather   # prompt tolerance, decode exact, dispatch list
	go test ./llm/ -run 'TestAttnGPU|TestGraphIsAChunkSplit|TestPrerecordedDecodeCrossesTheGatherBound'

**The engagement check had to be the dispatch list and not the answer.** The
first draft asserted "decode differs from the token rows, else it never
engaged", and it failed on a zero. That zero was the arithmetic, not a bug. The
split's sibling test (`TestAttnGPUGatherSplitIsTheGather`) cannot see this arm
at all: its 1e-4 is the fp16 store of the unsplit output, identical in both
arms to six places. So the gate asserts the zero, then reads `graph(0)`'s
kinds for one gather, no mask and one split.

`TestAttnGPUGatherSelectsTheSameCells` reads the token-tile layout through
`Gathered`, and now pins `SetHeadRows(false)`: its second chunk starts past the
bound. The arena is sized for whichever layout is larger.

## Where 128k prefill stands

ms a prefill token at 128 000 cells, ubatch 2048, from the labels:

	                 P14/P16   P17
	floor              0.818   0.818   everything flat in depth
	attn.attn          0.302   0.093
	attn.score         0.027   0.027
	attn.select        0.017   0.017
	gather + mask      0.010   0.002
	host gather        0.036   0.036   (see below)

The attention's depth terms are now **0.14 ms of a 0.99 ms token**. What is
left of the falloff is mostly the floor: `moe.up` alone is a quarter of the
token.

## Control arms

	LLM_ATTN_GATHER_HROWS=0        # P14/P15's token-row gathered kernel
	LLM_ATTN_GATHER_HROWS=1        # forced, at every depth (bypasses the rule)
	LLM_ATTN_GATHER_HROWS_MIN=<n>  # the prefill past bound, default selWidth
