# P17 — heads on the fragment's rows: 128k prefills past 1000 tok/s

**2026-09-22.** One change. A 128 000-cell prefill at ubatch 2048 goes
**833.5 → 1011.4 tok/s (1.21x)**, 64 000 cells **896.4 → 1048.6 (1.17x)**, and
the prefill falloff from depth zero goes from **0.72x to 0.88x**. Decode at depth gains
**~2%** because the mask pass is gone (31.62 → 32.21 tok/s at 128k), and a
decode step's answer is **bit-identical**.

| depth | pp before | pp after | | tg before | tg after |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 0 | 1156.6 | 1156.3 ¹ | 1.00x | 34.39 | 34.34 |
| 4 096 | 1015.4 | **1049.1** | 1.03x | 33.33 | **34.10** |
| 64 000 | 896.4 | **1048.6** | **1.17x** | 32.17 | **32.97** |
| 128 000 | 833.5 | **1011.4** | **1.21x** | 31.62 | **32.21** |

48 layers, shipped banks, `-pp 2048 -tg 16 -ctx 139000`, `wiki.test.raw`,
same binary, arms selected by `LLM_ATTN_GATHER_HROWS`. Two interleaved runs a
arm at 0/64k/128k (agreeing to 0.2%, the table is their mean:
`results/p17_ab48_h{0,1}_r{1,2}.csv`), one at 0/4096 with the default rule
against the control (`results/p17_rule_{def,0}.csv`).
¹ The default rule, which takes the token-row kernel at depth 0. Forcing the
heads build there (`LLM_ATTN_GATHER_HROWS=1`) is 1144.3, −1.1% — see below.

## The idea

P14's gathered attention puts sixteen consecutive **tokens** of one query head
on a cooperative-matrix fragment's M axis, and reads the **union** of their
QSA selections. At 128 000 cells that is 7 049 cells a tile where one token
selects 2 051. P14 called that 3.4x "the shape of the hardware against the
shape of QSA", something nothing in this vertical closes.

But the selection is per **token**, not per head, and this model has 24 query
heads over 2 kv heads. The twelve heads of one token are twelve rows that attend
over **exactly the same cells** of **exactly the same key and value**. Put them
on M instead:

- **The list is one token's selection**, 2 051 cells, not a sixteen-token
  union. The gather's existing `BM=1` build writes it (pass 1 only).
- **There is no per-row mask.** Every row wants every gathered cell, so the
  `attn.gathmask` dispatch is gone. The kernel's only predicate is `col < cnt`
  on a short last chunk.
- **The kv plane is staged once for twelve heads**, not once a head.
  That is the sharing P14's `HPW` knob tried, at 12x instead of 2x.
- **The Q fragment needs no repack.** The plane is head-major, tiled 16 tokens
  by 16 dims, so row `r` of (token t, dim group kt) is sixteen contiguous halves
  one head's plane apart: a RowMajor `coopMatLoad` with a stride of one head.

Rows are heads `h0 .. h0+15` with `h0 = min(g*rep, heads-16)`. The four rows
belonging to the other kv head are computed against the wrong key and never
stored, which is cheaper than any test inside the fragment and keeps every Q
load inside the plane. 12 of 16 rows are useful. Against the 2 051/7 049 the
token rows got at 128k, that is the whole win. The grid is (token, kv head),
or (token·splits + slice, kv head) split.

`attn.attn` at 128k, 48 layers: **51.6 → 15.9 ms a pass, 3.25x** (0.302 →
0.093 ms a token). On the 4-layer probe, whose one attention layer is denser
than the mean, it is 77.2 → 16.8 ms, 4.6x.

## Where it loses, and the rule

From a cold cache the selection names every live cell, so a token tile's union
*is* one row's, and heads-on-rows only wastes a quarter of the fragment. On the
4-layer probe (tok/s, two runs each, `results/p17_cross_h{0,1}.csv`):

	past        0     2048    4096    8192   16384  128000
	tokens  11109   10406   10162    9818    9424    7817
	heads   11076   10504   10590   10529   10500   10271

At 48 layers and ctx 139 000 the depth-0 loss is 1.1% (5.40 → 6.58 ms of
`attn.attn` a pass). So prefill takes heads-on-rows only when
`past >= selWidth` (`LLM_ATTN_GATHER_HROWS_MIN` overrides). Decode always
takes it once it gathers, because there the two builds are the same bits.

## Exactness

**Decode is bit-identical**, and the gate asserts a zero. At one row, the
token fragment's union *is* the token's selection, so both kernels fold the
same cells in the same chunks in the same order. A matrix product's rows are
independent, so which fragment row a head lands in does not change its sums. What
decode gains is the deleted mask dispatch (6.6 µs a layer) and a gather that
no longer ORs sixteen rows.

**Prefill is a reassociation**, like P14-2: the same set, folded in different
chunks. 3.6e-05 relative rms from the token-row kernel against 1.2e-02 of
either from llama.cpp, and against the block kernel 4.31e-06 where the token-row
gather is 4.10e-06. It falls under `PinSchedule` with the gather it rides on,
so nothing new there.

Gates:

	go test ./llm/ -run TestAttnGPUHeadRowsIsTheGather   # prompt tolerance, decode exact, dispatch list
	go test ./llm/ -run 'TestAttnGPU|TestGraphIsAChunkSplit|TestPrerecordedDecodeCrossesTheGatherBound'

**The engagement check had to be the dispatch list and not the answer.** The
first draft asserted "decode differs from the token rows, else it never
engaged", and it failed on a zero. That zero was the arithmetic, not a bug. The
split's sibling test (`TestAttnGPUGatherSplitIsTheGather`) cannot see this arm
at all: its 1e-4 is the fp16 store of the unsplit output, identical in both
arms to six places. So the gate asserts the zero, then reads `graph(0)`'s
kinds for one gather, no mask and one split.

`TestAttnGPUGatherSelectsTheSameCells` reads the token-tile layout through
`Gathered`, and now pins `SetHeadRows(false)`: its second chunk starts past the
bound. The arena is sized for whichever layout is larger.

## Where 128k prefill stands

ms a prefill token at 128 000 cells, ubatch 2048, from the labels:

	                 P14/P16   P17
	floor              0.818   0.818   everything flat in depth
	attn.attn          0.302   0.093
	attn.score         0.027   0.027
	attn.select        0.017   0.017
	gather + mask      0.010   0.002
	host gather        0.036   0.036   (see below)

The attention's depth terms are now **0.14 ms of a 0.99 ms token**. What is
left of the falloff is mostly the floor: `moe.up` alone is a quarter of the
token.

## Control arms

	LLM_ATTN_GATHER_HROWS=0        # P14/P15's token-row gathered kernel
	LLM_ATTN_GATHER_HROWS=1        # forced, at every depth (bypasses the rule)
	LLM_ATTN_GATHER_HROWS_MIN=<n>  # the prefill past bound, default selWidth

lines: | [P14](p14-prefill-at-depth.md) | **The gather, and 128k prefills past 900 tok/s — the target met.** A 128 000-cell prefill goes from P13's **563.6** to **826.0 tok/s at ubatch 2048** (1.47x, falloff from depth zero 0.50x → 0.72x) and to **946.1 at 8192**, with decode unmoved as the control. Four changes. **The selection runs over block scores, not cells**: all `ratio` cells of a pooled block carry one score, so a radix select over `nKV/ratio` entries with a per-block *weight* — how many of its cells this token can see, which is closed form — reaches the same threshold, the same tie fill and the same bitmask, and `llm_attn_expand.comp` is then not computed at all. `attn.select` **0.281 → 0.020 ms a token** (13.8x, not the 4x the traffic argument predicts: the histogram is bounded at the last block a cell can reach and the 16 KB LDS cache now holds `ratio` times as many cells), the expansion deleted, and **1.14 GB of arena** freed — bit-identical over four chunk schedules, including the ones that make the incomplete tail and the causal boundary inside a partly visible block both live. **The attention runs over a per-cell gather**: per query tile, the union of its rows' selections compacted ascending with the causal test folded into a per-row mask, then a *dense* attention over the list with no axis walk, no block skip and no causal comparison. **2.15x on `attn.attn`**, which is exactly the cell ratio — 15 145 cells read against a 7 049-cell union, measured with a new `SelUnion` instrument after P13's own estimate of both numbers turned out wrong. It needed **the value plane to become cell-major** first (a selected run is `ratio` consecutive cells, one 128-byte line; transposed it was four halves out of each of sixteen rows), which costs the block kernel 7% and decode nothing, and it stages one head-dim group at a time through 1 KB of LDS because occupancy is the one thing a prefill cannot trade. It is **the first kernel here that is not chunk-invariant and cannot be made so** — its list is the union of sixteen rows, so a chunk ending inside the tile folds the same terms in a different order — so it is pinned off under `PinSchedule` with the other reassociating kernels and gated by an *exact* equality on the set plus a tolerance on the answer (4.1e-06 rms against 9.9e-04 from llama.cpp). **The indexer's score moves to the matrix cores**, a GEMM per head with a rectifier: 0.077 → 0.034, chunk-invariant, and marginally nearer llama.cpp's own selection than the scalar kernel it replaces. **And `maxStorageBufferRange` gets an error instead of a comment**, because it is silent when exceeded: the driver clamps the descriptor rather than failing, so a five-depth sweep at ubatch 4096 raised `-ctx` past the cap, attended over a cache of zeros, and came back **1124 tok/s against a true 886** — 1.28x too fast, with a degenerate indexer selecting a contiguous window. *The failure mode is a benchmark that gets faster.* **Four measured refusals, and together they say what the gathered kernel is bound by**: doubling its matrix work costs **2.7%**, a subgroup staging barrier instead of a workgroup one is 1.00x, staging two head-dim groups a barrier is 1.00x (four is 0.75x), and sharing the staged key and value across two query heads of one kv head — halving both the global gather reads and the LDS writes — is **1.04x** (four heads is 0.75x). Not the matrix cores, not latency, not the gather's traffic: what is left is the LDS round-trip for the fragments and the per-head softmax scaffolding, both linear in the union, which is why the cost is linear in the cells visited. |

| [P16](p16-decode-arena-width.md) | **The wide batch never cost decode anything: two moves padded to the arena.** Decode **1.16x at every depth** at ubatch 2048 (29.73 → **34.4 tok/s** at depth zero, 27.20 → **31.5** at 128 000 cells), prefill flat, all three changes exact. **The cost P12-7 and P15 measured for a wide `-llm-batch` was a bug**: `DeltaNetGPU.InPort` and `AttnGPU.InPort` advertised the arena's rows, so every decode step zero-filled the whole prefill arena of both blocks' A operand once a layer — `move` 5.5 → 19.7 µs and the qkv projection behind it 1.9x at an 8192-row arena, found by staging wide arenas and prefilling narrow (`-depth -ubatch`), which showed the cost follows the arena and not the prefill. Padding to `roundUp(rows, rowAlign)` takes an 8192 arena's decode 23.55 → **33.87** (1.44x), and through the server decode is **34.2 tok/s at 2048, 4096 and 8192 alike** (P12-7: 28.04 and 25.81) — the break-even is gone. **`hc.cn` goes back to a stream a workgroup at decode** (25.0 → 7.0 µs, 1.06x of a token): P11's workgroup a token is one workgroup on forty CUs walking four streams in series. **`attn.select`'s emit walks blocks, not cells** (68 → 55 µs at 128k). Two refusals: batching the histogram's loads (0.96x) and folding same-bucket lanes before the atomic (0.69x). |

+| [P17](p17-heads-on-rows.md) | **Heads on the fragment's rows: 128k prefills past 1000 tok/s.** 833.5 → **1011.4 tok/s** at 128 000 cells and 896.4 → **1048.6** at 64 000, ubatch 2048 (falloff 0.72x → 0.88x); decode at depth +2%, bit-identical. The selection is per token and twelve query heads share each kv head, so a token's heads on M select the same cells against the same key: the gathered list is one token's 2 051 cells instead of a sixteen-token union of 7 049, the per-row mask dispatch is deleted, and the kv plane is staged once for twelve heads. Q needs no repack (a RowMajor load one head's plane apart). `attn.attn` 3.25x at 48 layers. Taken for prefill at `past >= selWidth` (it is −1.1% from a cold cache, where the union already is one row) and always at decode, where it is exact. |

| [P13](p13-long-context-prefill.md) | **128k completes, and the attention kernel's key block was twice as wide as it should have been.** A 128 000-cell prefill **runs**, for the first time in this vertical, at **471.7 tok/s** — and the thing stopping it was never `DispatchMultiMarked`'s marks, it was that **P0's submit budget had no depth term in it**. Every measurement behind P0's `322 us a dispatch + 582 ns a dispatch-row` was taken from cell zero, so `batchFor(rows)` went on handing back the same 660 dispatches at 2048 rows whether the cache was empty or held 128 000 cells; at 64 000 those 660 already held the gfx ring for ~1.53 s of the 2 s watchdog while the budget believed it was spending 0.86, and at ~115 000 they cross it. The missing term is **10.46 ns per (row, cell)** — read straight off P12's own ladder, 1.696 s a pass at depth zero against 3.067 at 64 000 — and **only the attention dispatches carry it**, because every other block is flat in depth (P11-5). So the chunker walks the recorded sequence and cuts where the *accumulated* prediction reaches the budget, charging each dispatch what its own label costs, and rescales itself against what the last submit actually measured — **upwards only**, because the affine constant is an order out at one row and a scale that learned from decode steps would hand the next prefill four times its budget. Then **the rung**: L2f chose `qt1_kt2` on 512-token prefills from cell zero, where a 32-cell key block is two cooperative-matrix tiles of reuse against one. At depth that is the wrong ladder — what the kernel can skip is a (query tile, key block) pair, so the cost is the *union* of sixteen adjacent queries' selections at the block's width, and P11-7's own table says 11.7% of the axis at 16 cells against 17.4% at 32. The new `qt1_kt1` build is **1.61x on `attn.attn` at 128 000 cells** (0.9107 → 0.5659 ms a token), 1.60x at 96 000, 1.36x at 64 000 and 1.19x at 32 000, with `attn.select`, `attn.score` and `attn.expand` identical to three decimals as the control — **471.7 → 563.6 tok/s**, falloff 0.42x → 0.50x, two passes agreeing to 0.05-0.2%. That is P11-7's 1.40x collected as a **rung** after P11-7 lost 1.18x trying to collect it as a branch, and it is the rule that file drew, applied: change the loop's granularity, not what happens inside it. It is **prefill's rung and not decode's** — with it on both, decode at 128k went 22.94 → 22.27, because a decode step costs one wave's serial walk (P8) and halving the block doubles the walk. **The refusal is the idea that looked best going in.** `llm_attn_blocks.comp` compacts the live key blocks into an ascending per-query-tile list so the kernel iterates the list instead of the axis — bit-identical, gated as an equality, deleting **83% of the visits** at 128 000 cells for 0.001 ms a token — and it is **1.00x at every depth**, and 1.05x *against* at the narrow rung where there are twice as many dead blocks to skip. The mask read was never the cost: the same sixteen lines serve all twenty-four heads and the MALL holds the tile's whole 128 KB. Third instance of one rule, now the engine's rather than any kernel's: *latency and redundant reads that matter at decode do not matter at prefill, because prefill has occupancy* — 3072 single-wave workgroups against a decode step's 24. It ships behind `LLM_ATTN_BLOCK_LIST=1` because the decode split and a per-cell gather both want it. **And the arithmetic of 900 tok/s at 128k is now closed-form**: the floor of everything flat in depth is 0.803 ms a token, `attn.attn` is 0.566, and `attn.select` + `attn.expand` are 0.284 and are one change; those plus a 4096 ubatch reach ~700, and **only the per-cell gather reaches 900** — priced at 2.8x on `attn.attn` where before P13 it needed 4.9x. |

| [P12](p12-prefill-round-two.md) | **Prefill round two: two bit-exact kernel changes, and four of P11's own leads measured away.** Prefill is **1.012-1.025x on both axes** — 1191.2 → **1207.7 tok/s** at 2048 rows, 1370.5 → **1403.9** at 8192 (**3.59x** llama.cpp), and 651.3 → **667.7** at 64 000 cells — with the two base passes agreeing to 1370.5/1370.5 and 651.3/651.2. Two changes hold. **The attention kernel's row max ran on sixteen lanes of sixty-four**: `for (i = lane; i < BM; i += WAVE)` with BM 16 and WAVE 64, KTIL times a block, two barriers and a store around each pass, each active lane then walking TILE cells serially with a `selected()` bit test. The whole key block is now staged at once (`stage` holds QT\*KTIL tiles, 2 KB of LDS) and RCL = WAVE/BM lanes share a row, folded by a **clustered subgroup max** — **bit-identical**, because a max has no rounding and the cells scanned are the same ones in the same order, and the wave is converged where the op is issued. **1.16x on the kernel at 512 tokens** and **+1.6-1.8% of a prefill token from 8000 cells on**. And **a K-quant block's header is one sixteen-byte load, not four dwords**: Q4_K/Q5_K open every block with `d`, `dmin` and twelve packed scale bytes, so at BK 32 a lane was issuing eight scalar loads a K-step against the nibbles' four `uvec4`s — L5b-7's rule for the third time. Every block of both formats is 16-byte aligned (region, row and block all multiples of 16) and `MoEGPU.build` now says so rather than trusting it; with the nibble extracted in two ops instead of four it is **`moe.up` 12 118 → 11 755 µs at 2048 tokens (1.031x)** with **`moe.down` (IQ4_NL, untouched) flat as the control**. **And four refusals, which close most of P11's open list.** **Both of `hc.cn`'s named suspects cost nothing**: deleting the 256-way reduction tree outright measures **5331.5 µs against 5325.8** — the eight barriers four times a token are **free**, so the non-bit-exact rewrite queued behind them would have bought zero — and replacing the per-token `gamma` read with a constant measures **5332.9**, because it is the same 40 KB every token and the MALL serves it. Its 57% of copy bandwidth is now unexplained *and* out of hypotheses. **The block skip hoisted out of the loop is 1.00x at every depth**: at 64k a query tile walks ~2000 blocks and skips ~1480, each paying a **dependent** global read, and a cost model where a dead block is ~20% of a live one reproduces `attn.attn`'s 9.8-against-16.0 TFLOP/s exactly — so the whole key range was voted on up front in one coalesced pass with a subgroup ballot, no atomics and no per-block barrier, and it bought **nothing**. The reason is the **exact converse of P8**: a decode step dispatches 24 single-wave workgroups and nothing hides a serial walk, but a 2048-token prefill dispatches **3072**, so that latency is already covered — *latency that matters at decode does not matter at prefill, because prefill has occupancy*. It is still live for decode, where it was deliberately never built. **The selection mask loop is 3.5-8%**, not the rest of the gap. **The MoE's per-element affine is a floor**: gutting the whole scale path is 1.21x at 2048 tokens, P12-2 takes the loads and integer ops out of that, and what remains — an int→float convert, an FMA and an f16 convert on every weight — has no bit-exact cheaper form, since packed fp16 costs thirteen bits of mantissa and `v_cvt_pkrtz` rounds the wrong way. **The ubatch remains the largest number on the board**: 2048 → 8192 is 1.16x and the curve has not flattened, which is a memory budget rather than a kernel. |

That is L5b-7's finding on the *operand* instead of the weight — the kernel is bound by how many load instructions it issues — so the halves arena is bound a second time as `uvec4` (binding 7) and a row is four aligned loads: **`moe.up` 14 918 → 11 936 µs a layer at 2048 tokens (1.25x)**, bit for bit the same slab, MODE 1 untouched as the control. The graph: **1079.6 → 1165.1 tok/s at 2048 rows, 1250.1 → 1328.5 at 8192 (3.40x llama.cpp)**, two runs agreeing to 0.2%. **Three changes that look right and are not**, all reverted, all one answer: a 16-row alignment with a row count per record (13.7 ms against 11.9 — the per-fragment branch inside the unrolled accumulator loops costs more than 35% of the rows, and the kernel goes to 256 VGPRs), three sub-lists one dispatch a rung (12.5 — no guard anywhere, but small grids do not fill the machine and three grids have three ramps), and a **128-row block** (13.5 — 608 tiles to 477 but the padding to 2.98x, because with 399 experts touched **the floor is one tile an expert** however wide the block). **At prefill this GEMM is bound by its per-tile slab unpack and the rows are very nearly free**; L5b built the padding as a cost to justify and it is not one, so the way in is fewer *tiles*, which is a bigger ubatch — which is the result. **A second round takes it to 3.51x.** `hc.cn` — the combine fused with the next mixer's norm, the second largest kernel in a prefill and one that does **no arithmetic** — was one workgroup per (token, stream), and the four streams of a token combine *the same* block output row: 110 KB a token where 80 would do. One workgroup a token, the output held in ten registers a thread already had spare, is **1.37-1.44x on the kernel** and bit-identical (each stream still reduces through the same 256-way tree), taking the graph to **1191.8 / 1372.2 tok/s** at 2048 / 8192 rows and 64k prefill to **654 tok/s** from 440. And `AttnGPU.SelSkip` measures, for the first time, **how much of the key axis the QSA selection actually lets the attention kernel skip**: at 64 000 cells the shipped 16x32 tile keeps **25.9%** of (query tile, key block) pairs live, a 16-cell tile would keep 18.5%, and a single query row 14.7% — so **a per-query gather is worth 1.76x, not the 31x the 3.2% density suggests**, which is L4b's "at prefill the density makes it pointless" with a number on it. The 1.40x between a 32-cell block and a 16-cell one was built as a bit-identical per-k-tile skip and is **1.18x slower** (866.1 → 737.2 tok/s at 16k), and at 64k slow enough to hold the ring past P0's two-second watchdog. Two kernels, one rule: **a branch inside an unrolled cooperative-matrix loop costs more than the work it removes** — neither kernel is arithmetic-bound, so change the loop's granularity, not what happens inside it. lines: +	// pleAhead is a PrefetchPLE still faulting pages in (P17). A gather waits
+	// for it rather than faulting the same pages beside it, and Destroy waits
+	// for it because it reads the model's mapping.
+// PrefetchPLE faults in the n-gram table's pages for `next`, the batch that
+// will follow `prev`, on a goroutine of its own, and returns at once (P17).
+// A prompt's rows are 16 a token at random offsets into a 28.80 GB mapping
+// that is mostly not in the page cache, so a fresh 2048-token chunk is ~32 000
+// major faults: **16 ms of host gather a chunk at depth 0, where the bench's
+// warm-up pass has touched the same text, and 93 ms at 32 000 cells, where it
+// has not** — 3-4% of a prefill pass, spent with the GPU idle. But a prompt's
+// tokens are all known before its first chunk runs, so the next chunk's faults
+// can be taken while the device works on this one, when the host is otherwise
+// waiting on a fence. The gather it does is discarded; what it leaves behind is
+// warm pages, and the real gather then reads them at ~12 µs a token.
+// It changes no value anywhere — the rows are the table's, whoever faulted
+// them — and a wrong guess costs page cache and nothing else. `prev` supplies
+// the n-gram's predecessors; only its last NGram-1 tokens are read.
// Prefill runs every layer over a prompt **as a fresh sequence**, leaving the
// wide residual in the hyper-connection block's arena.

2

11	|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|

17	48 layers, shipped banks, `-pp 2048 -tg 16 -ctx 139000`, `wiki.test.raw`,
18	same binary, arms selected by `LLM_ATTN_GATHER_HROWS`. Two interleaved runs a
19	arm at 0/64k/128k (agreeing to 0.2%, the table is their mean:
20	`results/p17_ab48_h{0,1}_r{1,2}.csv`), one at 0/4096 with the default rule
21	against the control (`results/p17_rule_{def,0}.csv`).
22	¹ The default rule, which takes the token-row kernel at depth 0. Forcing the
23	heads build there (`LLM_ATTN_GATHER_HROWS=1`) is 1144.3, −1.1% — see below.
24	
25	## The idea
26	
27	P14's gathered attention puts sixteen consecutive **tokens** of one query head
28	on a cooperative-matrix fragment's M axis, and reads the **union** of their
29	QSA selections. At 128 000 cells that is 7 049 cells a tile where one token
30	selects 2 051. P14 called that 3.4x "the shape of the hardware against the
31	shape of QSA", something nothing in this vertical closes.
32	
33	But the selection is per **token**, not per head, and this model has 24 query
34	heads over 2 kv heads. The twelve heads of one token are twelve rows that attend
35	over **exactly the same cells** of **exactly the same key and value**. Put them
36	on M instead:
37	
38	- **The list is one token's selection**, 2 051 cells, not a sixteen-token
39	  union. The gather's existing `BM=1` build writes it (pass 1 only).
40	- **There is no per-row mask.** Every row wants every gathered cell, so the
41	  `attn.gathmask` dispatch is gone. The kernel's only predicate is `col < cnt`
42	  on a short last chunk.
43	- **The kv plane is staged once for twelve heads**, not once a head.
44	  That is the sharing P14's `HPW` knob tried, at 12x instead of 2x.
45	- **The Q fragment needs no repack.** The plane is head-major, tiled 16 tokens
46	  by 16 dims, so row `r` of (token t, dim group kt) is sixteen contiguous halves
47	  one head's plane apart: a RowMajor `coopMatLoad` with a stride of one head.
48	
49	Rows are heads `h0 .. h0+15` with `h0 = min(g*rep, heads-16)`. The four rows
50	belonging to the other kv head are computed against the wrong key and never
51	stored, which is cheaper than any test inside the fragment and keeps every Q
52	load inside the plane. 12 of 16 rows are useful. Against the 2 051/7 049 the
53	token rows got at 128k, that is the whole win. The grid is (token, kv head),
54	or (token·splits + slice, kv head) split.
55	
56	`attn.attn` at 128k, 48 layers: **51.6 → 15.9 ms a pass, 3.25x** (0.302 →
57	0.093 ms a token). On the 4-layer probe, whose one attention layer is denser
58	than the mean, it is 77.2 → 16.8 ms, 4.6x.
59	
60	## Where it loses, and the rule
61	
62	From a cold cache the selection names every live cell, so a token tile's union
63	*is* one row's, and heads-on-rows only wastes a quarter of the fragment. On the
64	4-layer probe (tok/s, two runs each, `results/p17_cross_h{0,1}.csv`):
65	
66		past        0     2048    4096    8192   16384  128000
67		tokens  11109   10406   10162    9818    9424    7817
68		heads   11076   10504   10590   10529   10500   10271
69	
70	At 48 layers and ctx 139 000 the depth-0 loss is 1.1% (5.40 → 6.58 ms of
71	`attn.attn` a pass). So prefill takes heads-on-rows only when
72	`past >= selWidth` (`LLM_ATTN_GATHER_HROWS_MIN` overrides). Decode always
73	takes it once it gathers, because there the two builds are the same bits.
74	
75	## Exactness
76	
77	**Decode is bit-identical**, and the gate asserts a zero. At one row, the
78	token fragment's union *is* the token's selection, so both kernels fold the
79	same cells in the same chunks in the same order. A matrix product's rows are
80	independent, so which fragment row a head lands in does not change its sums. What
81	decode gains is the deleted mask dispatch (6.6 µs a layer) and a gather that
82	no longer ORs sixteen rows.
83	
84	**Prefill is a reassociation**, like P14-2: the same set, folded in different
85	chunks. 3.6e-05 relative rms from the token-row kernel against 1.2e-02 of
86	either from llama.cpp, and against the block kernel 4.31e-06 where the token-row
87	gather is 4.10e-06. It falls under `PinSchedule` with the gather it rides on,
88	so nothing new there.
89	
90	Gates:
91	
92		go test ./llm/ -run TestAttnGPUHeadRowsIsTheGather   # prompt tolerance, decode exact, dispatch list
93		go test ./llm/ -run 'TestAttnGPU|TestGraphIsAChunkSplit|TestPrerecordedDecodeCrossesTheGatherBound'
94	
95	**The engagement check had to be the dispatch list and not the answer.** The
96	first draft asserted "decode differs from the token rows, else it never
97	engaged", and it failed on a zero. That zero was the arithmetic, not a bug. The
98	split's sibling test (`TestAttnGPUGatherSplitIsTheGather`) cannot see this arm

100	arms to six places. So the gate asserts the zero, then reads `graph(0)`'s
101	kinds for one gather, no mask and one split.
102	
103	`TestAttnGPUGatherSelectsTheSameCells` reads the token-tile layout through
104	`Gathered`, and now pins `SetHeadRows(false)`: its second chunk starts past the
105	bound. The arena is sized for whichever layout is larger.

lastPrompt: Can you take a look at the LLM prompt processing and token generation speeds at long context. We want to push them as high as possible.

aiTitle: LLM prompt processing and token generation speeds

content.text:
At 128k, prompt processing went from **900 to 1176 tok/s** at the server's default batch of 4096 tokens (1.31x). Token generation went from 31.6 to 32.2 tok/s. Both runs of each arm agreed to within 0.2%. The tests I ran pass, `go build ./...` and `vet` are clean, and I haven't committed (the auto-committer will pick it up).

**Results** (full 48-layer model, shipped weights, before/after measured the same hour):

| context depth | prefill before | prefill after | generation before | generation after |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 0 | 1157 | 1156 | 34.4 | 34.3 |
| 64k | 896 | 1081 | 32.2 | 33.0 |
| 128k (batch 2048) | 834 | 1011 | 31.6 | 32.2 |
| 128k (batch 4096) | 900 | **1176** | 31.3 | 32.2 |

The 128k batch-2048 row has only the first change below. The 64k and 128k batch-4096 rows have both.

**Change 1: the attention kernel's rows are now query heads instead of tokens.** The kernel computes 16 rows at once. Those rows used to be 16 consecutive tokens, so it had to read every cell any of them selected: about 7,000 cells, where one token selects about 2,050. The model has 12 query heads per key/value head, and all 12 select exactly the same cells for a given token. Putting those heads on the rows means reading only that token's 2,050 cells, and it removes a whole masking step. The attention kernel is 3.25x faster at 128k.
- **At depth 0** it would be 1.1% slower, so it only switches on once the cache holds some past context. The depth-0 row above confirms the old kernel still runs there.
- **During generation** its output is bit-identical to before. The gain there comes from the deleted masking step.
- **Accuracy:** during prefill the change is 3.6e-05 away from the old kernel. Both are 1.2e-02 from llama.cpp.

**Change 2: the next chunk's lookup-table pages load while the GPU runs the current one.** A 28.8 GB n-gram table stays in host memory, and each fresh 2048-token chunk triggered about 32,000 slow disk page loads, 85 ms with the GPU idle. Prompt tokens are known in advance, so the server and the benchmark now load the next chunk's pages in the background. That's +3.1% at 64k, and it doesn't change any output values.

**Tried and dropped:**
- Asking the OS to read the whole table ahead of time did nothing.
- A fully pre-read table got pushed out of memory when the model loaded.

**Still open, in rough order of value:**
- **The same table lookup during generation costs about 1 ms of every ~30 ms token** (3–4%). It can't be prefetched, because it depends on the token just sampled. The fix is keeping the 29 GB table resident in RAM on the LLM machine, which is your call on memory.
- **The token-selection step costs 54 µs per layer at 128k.** I measured where that goes, and its first pass is the expensive one. Reworking it is worth about 1–2% of generation.
- **The rest of the time doesn't depend on context length.** The mixture-of-experts weights take a quarter of each prefill token, and earlier work found that kernel already close to its limits.

I didn't run the whole-model logits test (85 GB). Its 7-token prompt doesn't reach the code I changed.

The write-up is `research/p17-heads-on-rows.md`. `TODO.md`, the research index and my memory notes are updated, and the measurement CSVs are in `results/p17_*`. To turn either change off for comparison, set `LLM_ATTN_GATHER_HROWS=0` or `LLM_PLE_PREFETCH=0`.

a='## Control arms'
b='''## P17-3: the decode select, keys in registers and a 10-bit digit

`attn.select` at decode is one 1024-lane workgroup a token. At 128 000 cells
it was **54.0 µs a layer**, priced by compiling scratch copies with the
pass loop cut (a timing, not an answer): ~13 µs of emit and setup, **~17 µs
for the first radix pass and ~8 µs for each of the other three**. Two causes,
two changes, and both leave the bitmask exact:

- **Past `SEL_LDS` (4096 blocks) every pass re-read every score from global
  memory.** Now each lane holds its blocks' keys in registers, `KREG = 40` a
  lane, 40 960 blocks, past the cache's buffer-range cap. The row is read once.
- **The first digit was the exponent.** An `f2ui` key's top 8 bits are sign
  plus seven exponent bits, and a row of block scores shares one or two of
  them, so pass 1's atomics collided. The 1024-lane build now takes a 10-bit
  digit (10+10+10+2), which adds three mantissa bits to the first. The P10
  bucket search is one lane a bucket, and still fits.

4-layer probe, 128 000 cells, one layer, µs, two runs each:

	            decode        prefill (2048 rows)
	8-bit      53.9  54.0     2935  2944
	10-bit     48.7  47.8     2923  2921
	regs       54.7  49.4     3212  3077
	regs+10    43.6  43.9     3701  2774

Neither half pays alone and together they are 1.23x. Prefill is noisy with
the registers and does not need them (2048 workgroups have occupancy to hide
the loads), so **decode takes regs+10 and prefill takes 10-bit**
(`AttnGPU.selectPipe`).

48 layers, shipped banks, two interleaved runs each
(`results/p17_select_{base,def}_r{1,2}.csv`):

	            128k select (ms a token)   128k decode tok/s
	base         0.687  0.687               32.90  32.96
	P17-3        0.544  0.544               33.19  33.12      1.007x

Depth 0 is +0.004 ms a token of select (the 10-bit digit where the LDS
cache already holds the row), 0.01%, and prefill is flat.

**Exactness** is the existing gate, `TestAttnGPUSelectBlocksIsTheCellSelect`,
the block select's bitmask against the cell select's, bit for bit. Its 4k
fixture is 1024 blocks and would never leave the LDS cache, so a test-only
build with `SEL_LDS=64` (`LLM_ATTN_SELECT_VARIANT=kreg_r10_lds64`) sends it down
the register path. A copy of that build with every register key zeroed
**fails** the gate, so the gate sees the path.

## Control arms'''

s=s.replace(a,b)
s=s.replace('''	LLM_PLE_PREFETCH=0             # P17-2's control''','''	LLM_PLE_PREFETCH=0             # P17-2's control
	LLM_ATTN_SELECT_VARIANT=base   # P17-3's control (P14-1's 8-bit select)
	LLM_ATTN_SELECT_VARIANT=r10|kreg|kreg_r10|kreg_r10_lds64''')

content.text:
I worked through both remaining items. One became a small, measured decode gain. The other turned out to be a different problem from the one I'd described, and I can't fully fix it without root on this machine.

**Token selection during generation (fixed, P17-3).** At 128k, this step drops from 54.0 to 43.8 µs per layer. Generation goes from **32.93 to 33.16 tok/s (+0.7%)** at 128k, and two interleaved full-model runs per arm agree. Prefill and depth 0 are unchanged, and its output is bit-identical.
- **The cause:** once the context passes about 16k tokens, the step re-read every block score from memory on each of its four passes. Its first pass was also slow because the top 8 bits of a float are mostly the exponent, so nearly every score landed in the same one or two buckets.
- **The fix:** each lane now loads its scores into registers once. On top of that, the 1024-lane build uses 10-bit radix digits, which spread the first pass across 1024 buckets.
- **Where each part runs:** neither half helps much alone. Together they apply only during generation. Prefill uses the 10-bit digits alone, because the register version was noisy there and doesn't need them.
- **Checking the test really exercises it:** the existing exactness test's fixture never reached the register path, so I added a test-only build that forces it. A deliberately broken copy of that build fails the test.

**The ~1 ms n-gram table lookup per generated token (diagnosed, not fixed).** Last time I called this a memory decision. It's mostly something else:
- **Where the time goes:** the typical step takes 236 µs. But 2 of every 32 steps take about 8.7 ms, at the same token positions in two separate runs, and those two steps are **75% of the total**.
- **What it isn't:** the slow steps take the same number of disk page loads as fast ones, and no garbage collection runs during them. I couldn't reproduce them in a standalone program either.
- **What's left:** it's somewhere in the kernel's page-fault handling, and tracing that needs root, which this account doesn't have. It's worth about 0.5 ms a token (~1.8%).
- **The fix available now:** keeping the 29 GB table in RAM would remove it, and that's still your call on the LLM machine's memory.

What's left in selection is about 13 µs of fixed overhead per layer, so there's not much more to take there. The P17 write-up, `TODO.md` and my memory notes are updated. `LLM_ATTN_SELECT_VARIANT=base` restores the old kernel for comparison.

---
name: ai-service-user-unit
description: "The ai server runs as a --user systemd unit on :11434; logs are journalctl --user -u ai, deploy.sh installs it, startup takes ~25 s, and it is deliberately served open with -token=."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
---

The `serve` binary runs as a **user** systemd unit, not a system one, and not
in the foreground:

- **Install/redeploy: `./deploy.sh`.** It builds `./ai` from `./cmd/serve`,
  substitutes the unit's `###` placeholder with `$(pwd)`, writes
  `~/.config/systemd/user/ai.service`, `daemon-reload`s and restarts.
  `./ai.service` in the repo is a *template*, not a script — running it gives
  `Permission denied`, which is the expected outcome, not a bug to fix.
- **`deploy.sh` ends with `journalctl --user -n 100 -f -u ai`,** which never
  returns. In an agent session run its steps by hand and skip the tail.
- **Logs: `journalctl --user -u ai`** (`--user` is required; it is invisible to
  the system journal). The server logs one line per backend at startup and
  `listening on http://0.0.0.0:11434` when all of them are up.
- **Startup is ~25 s** and ~13 GB peak, nearly all of it the Z-Image backend;
  tts/stt/embed land in the first 3 s. Don't conclude anything from the log
  before the image line.
- **State without tailing:**
  `systemctl --user show ai.service -p ActiveState -p SubState -p NRestarts`.
  The unit ships `Restart=always` + `RestartSec=1`, and the server `log.Fatal`s
  on any bad flag or missing checkpoint, so a config mistake becomes a silent
  ~26 s crash loop. A non-zero `NRestarts` (or "restart counter is at N" in the
  journal) is the tell; `systemctl --user reset-failed ai.service` before a
  fixed redeploy so the count reads clean.
- **Auth: omitting `-token` does not disable it.** The flag *defaults* to a
  non-empty token (`defaultToken` in `cmd/serve/main.go`), so a unit that says
  nothing about tokens requires a bearer header on every `/v1` request. Only an
  explicitly empty `-token=` opens the server. This cost an afternoon once.
- **The deployed unit runs `-token=` on purpose**, chosen 2026-09-18: open, no
  bearer header, on `0.0.0.0:11434` so the second machine can reach it. Don't
  "fix" the empty token back to a default — it is the configuration that was
  asked for. See [[deployment-two-machines]].
- The unit is **`disabled`** as of 2026-09-18 — it does not come back on boot
  or login without `systemctl --user enable ai` and `loginctl enable-linger`.

Anchor journal reads to the *current* instance
(`journalctl --user -u ai --since "@$(date -d "$(systemctl --user show
ai.service -p ExecMainStartTimestamp --value)" +%s)"`). A plain `--since -2min`
still contains the previous instance's crash lines and will make an
until-loop fire on a failure that is already fixed — the same self-matching
trap as [[watch-loops-must-not-match-themselves]]. See
[[deployment-two-machines]] for which box this is meant to run on and
[[gpu-debugging-access]] for when it hangs rather than exits.

name: deployment-two-machines
description: "Deployment is two Strix Halo machines — LLM on one, the other four verticals on the other — so no cross-vertical footprint work is needed."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: c757bc7f-8b16-44a4-983d-3e1e9e5bd863
  modified: 2026-09-17T23:32:36.559Z
---

Stated by Oliver 2026-09-18: the deployment target is **two** AI MAX+ 395
machines, not one. The qwen3.8-flash-next LLM (~80 GB resident) runs alone on
one; the image/speech/embedding verticals share the other. Consequently:

**Why:** the five-verticals-in-one-process residency problem does not exist,
and quantising z-image (or the other small models) for footprint is not
wanted — the DiT is compute-bound anyway (§3.4), so bits buy no speed.

**How to apply:** don't propose quantisation or memory-coexistence work for
the non-LLM verticals; `research/zimage-vertical.md`'s "What is not planned" section records the
decision. [[phase-2-pivot-to-pipeline]]

# P18 — the full trained context: 262 144 cells

**2026-09-22.** The model is trained to 262 144 tokens
(`qwen4exp.context_length`), and the server could hold about 148k of them.
The KV cache shared one fp16 arena with the prefill activations, and
`maxStorageBufferRange` is 4 GiB - 4. It now holds all 262 144, and the answer
is checked there, not just the rate:

- **Perplexity over positions 131 072-262 143 of one 262 144-token window:
  4.0344 ± 0.024** (`-ppl -ctx 262144 -chunks 1 -ubatch 4096 -head-rows 2048`,
  5m27s, `results/p18_ppl_262144.txt`). Every scored token reads the cache past
  the old cap. A cache that read back zeros there — the failure P14 found is
  silent — would not score 4.03.
- **Recall through the server:** a 237 286-token prompt (the first 1.03 MB of
  `wiki.test.raw`) asking who the *first* article is about. It answers
  **"Robert Boulter"**, which is the first line of the file. Prefill averaged
  **1022.3 tok/s** over the whole prompt, and decode ran at **29.86 tok/s at
  237k deep** (`results/p18_serve_262144.txt`).

## The change

The key plane, the value plane and the indexer's raw and pooled keys each get
a buffer of their own (`AttnGPU.kbuf/vbuf/ibuf`, bindings 8, 9 and 10 in
`llm_common.glsl`). Over twelve layers that is 12 KB, 12 KB and 3.8 KB a cell,
so the trained context is 3.22 + 3.22 + 0.81 GB, and K and V reach the range
at ~349k cells. The five kernels that touch the cache read and write it
through the new bindings: `pack` (writes K, V and the raw index key), `idx`
(pools the raw keys; the pooled key goes to the cache and the query to the
arena), both `score` builds, and `wmma` (K and V, through `coopMatLoad` and the
gather's `stagePlane`). Offsets are unchanged in meaning, just relative to
the new buffers. Every attention pipeline binds 0-10, with the bank padding
slots 5-7. Binding 5 was already the bank for the quantised GEMMs and the
GEMV, so `gemmBufs` is now the same list.

Two supporting changes:

- **`vk/shim.c`'s `SHIM_MAX_BINDINGS` 8 → 16.** Pipeline creation failed with
  `VkResult(-3)` at 11 bindings. It is a stack array bound, nothing more.
- **`cmd/llm -ppl -ubatch N`**: a window wider than any arena is prefilled in
  `N`-token batches (with P17-2's prefetch), and the scored half goes
  through `ExtendRows` a head-arena at a time. On the 4-layer prefix at a
  4096 window it agrees with the one-pass path to 2e-5. `-chunks N` now
  needs N windows of corpus, not llama.cpp's two, so one 262 144-token window
  fits `wiki.test.raw`'s 297 193 tokens.

The cap check (P14's `checkBufferRange`) now runs per buffer, and its message
names the per-plane limit.

## Gates

	go test ./llm/ -run 'TestAttnGPU|TestGraphIsAChunkSplit|TestPrerecordedDecode|TestInPortPadsTheRunNotTheArena|TestSpec|TestRewind|TestSnapshot'

All pass unchanged, including the exact ones (cache size, chunk split, the
rollback snapshot of the pooled keys, which now reads `ibuf`). Moving a plane
between buffers changes no arithmetic.

## The served configuration

`ai.service`'s LLM line: `-llm -llm-ctx 262144 -llm-batch 8192`. It stages in
**1m05.7s at ~83 GB**, leaving ~33 GB available on the 117 GB machine.
Batch 8192 because P16 showed a wider batch costs decode nothing and it is the
faster prefill for exactly the prompts this context exists for. At 262 144
cells it fits both the fp32 arena (the indexer's scores are 8192 x 65 536
floats, 2.1 GB) and the range. 4-layer probe at 248 000 cells, ubatch 4096:
prefill 0.86x of depth zero, decode 0.98x.

**Not changed:** `-llm-max-tokens` stays 1024. It is what a request that names
no `max_tokens` gets, a product choice rather than a rate, and this model
reasons before it answers.
EOF

---
name: watch-loops-must-not-match-themselves
description: "Never match a background process with `pgrep -f`/`pkill -f <substring>` — the invoking shell's own command line contains the substring, so the loop sees itself and `pkill` kills the shell."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: afdec50f-0d5d-434b-ab40-987d57291d76
  modified: 2026-09-13T22:16:50.419Z
---

Waiting on a long background command (e.g. a `go run ./cmd/bench` run) with
`until ! pgrep -f 'exe/bench'; do sleep 10; done` hangs forever: the watcher's
own `bash -c ... pgrep -f 'exe/bench' ...` command line matches the pattern, so
the loop sees itself and never terminates. The user had to interrupt to unstick
it, twice over — a second watcher then matched the first one too.

**Why:** `pgrep -f` matches the full command line of every process, including
the shell that is running the poll loop.

The same trap kills rather than hangs: `pkill -f 'serve -addr 127.0.0.1:18080'`
issued from a shell whose command line contains that string terminates the
shell itself (exit 144, the rest of the command never runs).

**How to apply:** wait on a completion marker instead of on a process — run the
command in the foreground with a generous `timeout`, or poll the log for its
final line (`grep -q 'wrote .* results' run.log`). If a process check is
genuinely needed, match the executable name exactly (`pgrep -x bench`) or
exclude self (`pgrep -f pattern | grep -v $$`). To stop a server you started,
write its PID to a file when you launch it and `kill $(cat pidfile)`. See [[strix-halo-bench-runs]].

content.text:
The LLM line in `ai.service` is now set for the model's full trained context of 262,144 tokens:

```
;ExecStart=###/ai -addr 0.0.0.0:11434 -token= -llm -llm-ctx 262144 -llm-batch 8192
```

**It needed a code change first.** The server capped out at about 148k tokens, because the context's memory shared one GPU buffer with other working data, and a single buffer can only be addressed up to 4 GiB. I moved that memory into three buffers of its own. The full 262k is now 7.3 GB and the new ceiling is about 349k. I also had to raise a fixed limit on GPU buffers per kernel (8 → 16) in the Vulkan wrapper.

**Checked on the answers, not just the speed:**
- **Scoring tokens beyond the old limit:** over positions 131k–262k of one full-length window, perplexity is **4.0344**, the same as every short-context measurement of this model. If that memory had read back wrong past the old limit, this would have blown up.
- **A 237,286-token prompt through the server:** asked who the very first article is about, it answered **"Robert Boulter"**, the first line of the text. Prompt processing averaged **1,022 tok/s**, and generation ran at **29.9 tok/s** at that depth.
- The existing attention and rollback tests all still pass.

**Why these two settings:**
- **Context 262144** is the full length the model was trained for.
- **Batch 8192** gives the fastest prompt processing on long prompts, and earlier work showed it costs generation nothing. At full context the server starts in about 66 seconds and uses ~83 GB, leaving ~33 GB free.
- **Not changed:** the default 1,024-token cap for requests that don't set `max_tokens`. That's a product choice, not a speed setting, though this model reasons before answering and can burn through it.

**Not deployed.** In this checkout the template's active line serves the other four models, and the unit is disabled here, so I only changed the template. On the LLM machine, uncomment that line (and comment out the other one), then run `./deploy.sh`.

To make the full-length check possible I also added a `-ubatch` option to the perplexity tool, for windows longer than the batch size. The write-up is `research/p18-full-context.md`, and `TODO.md`, the research index and my memory notes are updated. I haven't committed; the auto-committer will pick it up.
